member.name: M:Sim.Core.Analytics.EditableBodyPose.ToBoatState
member.summary: Build the consumed by the force-evaluation helper. When is true (default), the authored velocity triples are treated as already in world frame — the boat's orientation does not rotate them. This is usually what you want: heeling the boat shouldn't rotate the boat's translational motion through the water. Set false to interpret the values as body-frame (forward/lateral/vertical relative to the heeled hull).

member.name: T:Sim.Core.Appendage.AppendageInputs
member.summary: Per-tick sailor controls for the underwater appendages, consumed by every instance.

remarks.para: HelmAngle_rad is the rudder's actual stock angle — the value the hydrodynamics solve at — set by the sim each tick from the integrated RudderState. It is not the sailor's raw demand; that demand is , the target rudder angle a stiff hand holds the blade to. Convention: positive helm angle = trailing edge to port (+y in body frame) = bow yaws to port. This matches a real tiller pushed to starboard (rudder swings to port). The haptic feedback the sailor feels is reported back as AppendageState.StockTorque_Nm on the value returned by .
CenterboardRetraction ∈ [0, 1]: 0 = fully deployed (deepest immersion); 1 = fully out of the water. Real-time control on dinghies with a daggerboard; clamp at the model.
Models ignore inputs they don't care about — a keel ignores helm angle; a rudder ignores retraction.

member.name: T:Sim.Core.Appendage.AppendageState
member.summary:
Per-appendage state record produced by an each tick. Per design-doc §16.3, is a descriptive label only — runtime dispatch (e.g. "find the rudder's tiller torque") is via index bindings in scenario config (§17.5, §18.4), never by string match.
Per §21, the record carries split parasitic / induced drag, buoyancy magnitude, and the geometric inputs the renderer / diagnostics consume to sanity-check the new model. Existing is the sum of parasitic + induced for backwards compatibility with consumers that only want the lump.
Per §20.2 the record also carries the appendage's in its appendage-local frame and its rotation (helm angle for the rudder; identity for the daggerboard whose retraction is captured in ). These feed each tick.
is the raw commanded stock rotation (rudder; 0 for a fixed foil) — unlike , it doesn't require flow to read meaningfully, so it's the AI's sensing of weather helm at any boat speed, not just once the rudder is loaded.
self-describes an appendage that runs its own stock- rotation integrator (the rudder DOF) — must fold it in as a point mass (mass + parallel-axis only, no spin tensor) so the blade's rotational inertia isn't double-counted between the boat aggregate and its own integrator, mirroring the boom carve-out.

member.name: T:Sim.Core.Appendage.FoilCut
member.summary: A parsed foil-cut file — the 2-D source of truth for a foil. It is authored as two equal-length lists of [aft, down] points (root → tip), one per edge, with rake intrinsic to the coordinates (the leading edge drifts aft as it descends — there is no separate rake field), plus the NACA section, the dry head/bottom, and the foil's motion axes (rotation/retraction). Each LE/TE pair is a strip boundary, so the strip count comes from the cut (strips = stations − 1), exactly like the sail's panels. Mirrors : the model only places the cut (a root-attach point in the body frame), as mast placement lives in the rig rather than the sail cut. Authored in millimetres by default (handbook-native); units may be "m".
member.remarks:
Canonical origin. The root leading edge is the cut origin (le[0] = [0, 0]) — the foil analogue of the sail tack at (0,0). Every cut shares this origin, which is what makes cuts swappable against a fixed placement.
The JSON-mapped properties are set, not init, and that is load-bearing. Source generation cannot call an init accessor, so it emulates one as a constructor parameter and assigns every such property on every construction — an omitted key then overwrites the property initializer with default(T). The rudder cut omits topEdge and would silently load null (see SailCutSparseJsonTests).
The setters are internal, and that is load-bearing too. and are process-wide singletons that every boat's foils are built from, so a public setter would let any consumer re-plan every blade in the sim. init used to prevent exactly that and cannot be used here, so the accessor is narrowed instead of opened. [JsonInclude] is what lets source generation reach a non-public accessor; without it the generator skips the property entirely and the cut loads empty.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Appendage.ImmersedSegment.StripCentroid(System.Int32,System.Int32)
member.summary: World-frame centroid of the i-th of n evenly-spaced strips along the wetted segment. Strips are open intervals — strip 0 spans [0, 1/n], its centroid sits at 1/(2n) of the way from Start_W to End_W. Caller is responsible for 0 ≤ i < n.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Appendage.ImmersedSegment.ClipFromAbove(System.Single)
member.summary: Additionally clip this segment from above by a world-frame Z ceiling (§15.5 hull-bottom shielding). Any portion of the segment with Z > ceilingZ_W is removed. Used by foil components to model the fact that a daggerboard's in-trunk portion sees no flow, and a rudder's portion above the hull bottom is in the hull's wake — neither generates useful lift or buoyancy. The remaining segment retains its tip and trims its top. Returns if the whole segment is above the ceiling.

member.name: T:Sim.Core.Appendage.FoilGeometry
member.summary: Station-based foil planform geometry (design-doc §8 / §15 / §21). A foil is a list of spanwise stations — each a leading-edge ("luff") point, trailing-edge ("leech") point, and NACA thickness ratio — in a component-local frame, ordered root → tip. This supersedes the rectangular-prism (scalar span × chord × mean-thickness) v1: planform area, aspect ratio, displaced volume, wetted area, and the section-integrated inertia tensor all derive from the real planform + true NACA section, and the renderer consumes the same geometry as its mesh source of truth.

remarks.para: Local frame & reference line. Stations live in a body-aligned local frame whose origin is . The span line is the leading-edge (luff) line — the line the strip solver walks and applies forces along (the keel applies lift on this line; the rudder offsets aft by its stock-to-CoP distance). is the unit root→tip direction (rake baked in for keel/rudder). Helm is NOT baked into the stations: chord length is helm-invariant, so helm is applied at runtime (solver world chord direction, inertia LocalToBody quaternion, render pivot), keeping this geometry cacheable.
Span parametrisation. Span fraction f ∈ [0,1] runs root (0) → tip (1). /// interpolate linearly between bracketing stations. Volume/area/inertia integrate along the span projection onto .

member.name: T:Sim.Core.Boat.Boom
member.summary: Dynamic 2-DOF rigid body modeling the boom, per spanwise-rig spec §3. The boom hinges at the gooseneck (), integrates angular momentum via semi-implicit Euler at sim tick rate, and enforces sheet and vang as one-sided linear springs with stretch-rate damping.

remarks.para: Owns boom state across ticks. Constructed once per . The legacy (BoomCoupling-off) path calls exactly once per sim tick after all sails have produced their per-tick contributions. The coupled (BoomCoupling-on) path instead calls once (to contribute to the ArticulatedSolver) then once (to integrate the solved joint acceleration). Either way the boom advances exactly once per tick.
The field uses boom-local frame conventions for and (interpreted as moments about the gooseneck). See spec §3.5.
Pose convention (spec §3.2): at (Yaw=0, Pitch=0) the boom points aft along body −x, horizontal. Positive Yaw rotates the boom-end toward port (+y); positive Pitch rotates the boom-end downward (−z).

Convention sign flips: because positive Yaw equals port-ward motion (which is a left-hand rotation about body +z), the yaw torque drives the rate via YawRate += -τ_z / I_yaw · dt. Similarly the pitch axis at yaw ψ is (−sin ψ, −cos ψ, 0) so that positive pitch corresponds to boom-end down.

member.name: P:Sim.Core.Boat.Boom.SheetCrewPullMax_N
member.summary: Maximum tension the crew can ESTABLISH BY HAULING the mainsheet, in newtons (≈ max arm-pull × purchase ratio). This is a limit on TRIMMING IN, not on the force a cleated line transmits: once cleated, the boom can load the line far past this (up to the line/hardware's structural strength), so the reactive spring force is NOT capped here — the crew-pull figure only bounds the trim-in step (see the cleat reconciliation in ComputeTorqueAndDamping). = no trim limit (the legacy behaviour for tests that don't model crew strength).

member.name: P:Sim.Core.Boat.Boom.VangCrewPullMax_N
member.summary: Maximum tension the crew can establish by hauling the vang (max arm-pull × vang purchase). Limits trimming in, not the cleated line's reactive force. See .

member.name: P:Sim.Core.Boat.Boom.SheetLimits

member.name: P:Sim.Core.Boat.Boom.SheetTwoBlock_m

The commanded length is clamped to [TwoBlock, Stopper] in every code path, so passing means "eased to the stopper knot," not "sheet off."

What the boom hangs on the gooseneck hinge, body frame. Quasi-statically the hinge carries whatever the boom's other forces don't, so this is their sum — the sheet and vang pulls plus the boom's own weight. is the same world-frame vector handed to .
The clew force is deliberately absent. It shares the segment-0 leech tension the sail already publishes to the mast, so including it here would double-count that tension — which also means this omits the boom-compression thrust, the dominant real-world mast-bending mechanism.

member.name: T:Sim.Core.Boat.ControlLine
member.summary: One running-rigging control line (mainsheet or vang). Owns its travel limits, crew-pull trim reconciliation, and the scalar engagement curve mapping the controlled distance to the force delivered to the boom. Pure of boom geometry — supplies distances and applies the returned magnitude along the line direction.

remarks.para: The engagement curve is a softplus blend of the axial spring with a slack "catenary" shoulder whose amplitude scales with purchase and line weight. With lineWeight == 0 it reduces exactly to the legacy one-sided hinge max(k·(L−cleat), 0), which makes wiring it into the boom a behavior-preserving refactor. With lineWeight > 0 the engagement becomes a smooth, monotonic, C¹ ramp — the structural cure for slack↔taut leech chatter.

This is a catenary-motivated blend (heavier line / more purchase ⇒ softer, earlier engagement), not the exact small-sag 1/√ε form; see docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-11-control-line-catenary-engagement-design.md §5.

member.name: P:Sim.Core.Boat.ControlLine.AxialStiffness_N_per_m
member.summary: Effective taut stiffness (boom force per metre of stretch past the cleat), in N/m.

member.name: P:Sim.Core.Boat.ControlLine.Purchase
member.summary: Purchase / mechanical-advantage ratio (P). Softens the catenary and multiplies the delivered force. 1 = direct (no purchase).

member.name: P:Sim.Core.Boat.ControlLine.LineWeight_N_per_m
member.summary: Line + lumped-block weight per metre (w), in N/m. Sets the catenary engagement softness; 0 ⇒ the legacy hard hinge.

member.name: F:Sim.Core.Boat.ControlLine.DefaultEngagementShape
member.summary:
Engagement compliance (m²/N): sets the knee width δ = Shape·P·w (metres), the travel over which the line stiffens from slack to taut. Deliberately independent of the cleat (eased) length — the knee is a property of the line's compliance, not of how far it is paid out; scaling it by the eased length wrongly gives a long-eased line a wide knee and a large pre-load.
NOTE (live-tuning knob): a light, stiff line's bare catenary force is only a few N, so a physics-pure knee (≈ force/stiffness) would be microns wide — effectively still a hard hinge. This constant widens the knee to a meaningful cm scale, representing the combined give of catenary straightening + line/block/system compliance. The seed (0.0067 m²/N) yields a ~1.5 cm vang / ~0.5 cm sheet knee. The tradeoff: a wider knee raises the pre-load at the cleat (≈0.7·k·δ). Vetted live.

member.name: P:Sim.Core.Boat.ControlLine.EngagementShape
member.summary: Live-tunable backing for the engagement compliance (see summary above). Settable so the workbench can sweep the catch softness; 0 recovers the legacy hard hinge.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Boat.ControlLine.Force(System.Single,System.Single)
member.summary: Force (N) the cleated line delivers to the boom along the line direction at the given controlled distance. Slack→catenary shoulder, taut→axial; C∞, monotonic increasing. With == 0 this is the legacy hinge max(k·(L−cleat), 0).
member.param: Current geometric controlled distance L, in metres.
The cleated rest length (from ), in metres.

member.name: P:Sim.Core.Boat.ControlLine.KneeWidth_m
member.summary: Knee width (metres): the travel over which slack→taut stiffens. A constant of the line (not of the distance or the cleat) so is manifestly C∞ and monotonic. Zero ⇒ legacy hinge, which is what LaserDefaults ships.

member.name: P:Sim.Core.Boat.ControlLine.Limits
member.summary: What a controller is told about this line — the pull cap, the purchase, and the engagement curve's constants, so it can command a tension rather than a length.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Boat.ControlLine.Tautness(System.Single,System.Single)
member.summary: How taut the line is at this distance, in [0, 1] — the local engagement stiffness normalised by the axial stiffness (dF/dL / k, the softplus derivative = logistic sigmoid). → 0 (exponentially) when slack, 0.5 at the cleat, → 1 when taut. Used to scale the line's dashpot damping so an essentially-slack line does not drag the boom with its full damping. With == 0 this is the legacy step gate (1 past the cleat, else 0).

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Boat.ControlLine.CleatForForce(System.Single,System.Single)
member.summary:
The cleat length that would deliver at the given geometric distance — the exact inverse of . Lets a controller command a TENSION and let the boom decide how much line runs out, rather than commanding a length and discovering the tension.
Why that matters: on the shipped hard hinge the whole 0–375 N crew-pull range spans 3.75 mm of cleat travel on a line with 3.9 m of range, so boom motion of a millimetre reads as the tension collapsing and re-catching.
Travel limits are NOT applied — owns those.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Boat.ControlLine.ReconcileCleat(System.Nullable{System.Single},System.Single,System.Single)
member.summary: Reconcile the cleated rest length for this tick: clamp the commanded target to the travel limits [TwoBlock, Stopper], then apply the crew-pull trim-in limit — when hauling in (target shorter than the current cleat) the crew can shorten only to lineLength − CrewPull/k, and never past the existing cleat. Easing out or holding a cleated line while the boom loads it is unrestricted (the uncapped reactive force carries it). With CrewPull == ∞ trimming is free. Stateless — the caller stores the result.

member.name: T:Sim.Core.Boat.ControlLineLimits
member.summary:
What a controller needs to know about a control line: how hard the crew can haul it, what the purchase turns that haul into, and the force-versus-stretch curve relating the two ends. The controlled distance moves at the hauled length divided by , and hauling stops once tension reaches .
Grouped rather than left as sibling floats because none answers a question alone — a pull cap says nothing about line speed without the purchase to divide by, and neither says anything about what tension a commanded length will produce.
The curve lives here rather than only on because a controller reading an observation cannot see the line itself, and commanding a line by LENGTH is badly conditioned: on the Laser's mainsheet the whole 0–375 N range spans under 4 mm of a 3.9 m control. Given a controller can ask for a tension instead and let the boom decide how much line runs out.

member.name: F:Sim.Core.Boat.ControlLineLimits.Unlimited
member.summary: A line with no crew-pull cap, hauled directly. What a boat rigged without limits reports, and what leaves a hauling model running at its slack-line rate forever.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Boat.ControlLineLimits.Engagement(System.Single,System.Single,System.Single)
member.summary: Force a cleated line delivers at past its cleat: a softplus shoulder blending slack to axial, or the one-sided hinge max(k·x, 0) when the knee is zero (which is what LaserDefaults ships). Shared by so the curve and its inverse can never drift apart.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Boat.ControlLineLimits.StretchForForce(System.Single,System.Single,System.Single)
member.summary: The stretch that delivers — the exact inverse of , which is monotonic. Negative for a lightly loaded line (the cleat sits slacker than the line's own length).

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Boat.ControlLineLimits.CleatForForce(System.Single,System.Single)
member.summary: The cleat length that would deliver at this geometric distance. Travel limits are NOT applied — the caller owns those, and clamping here would hide that the tension asked for is unreachable on this hardware. Zero stiffness (an unrigged line) returns the distance unchanged rather than dividing into an infinity.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Boat.ControlLineLimits.ForceAtCleat(System.Single,System.Single)
member.summary:
What tension a commanded cleat implies at this geometric distance. Lets a controller read back its OWN command rather than the measured tension, which on a hinge-engaged line swings between zero and hundreds of newtons as the boom moves a millimetre.
Capped at , because a COMMANDED length is not necessarily a cleat: hauling is limited to length − CrewPullMax/k, so a command wound in against a loaded boom runs far below the cleat the line is really holding. Uncapped, this reads that gap as tension — a command at two-block with the boom a metre out computes 91 kN, two orders of magnitude past anything a crew can establish, and anything pacing itself off that number stalls for minutes.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Boat.ControlLineLimits.EasedCleat(System.Single,System.Single,System.Single)
member.summary:
Give away of the tension currently implies, and return the cleat that delivers what is left. The one way to ease a line: commanding a length instead overshoots the force band in a tick and banks slack the boom then accelerates across and snatches against.
Never shortens. A cleat already slacker than the boom has taken up has no tension to give away, and the length that would deliver "less" sits far SHORTER than where it is — so an unguarded conversion would haul in hard exactly when asked to ease.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Boat.ControlLineLimits.CanCommandTension(System.Single)
member.summary: Whether this line reports enough to invert its curve. A bench fixture or an unrigged boat has no stiffness and no geometry, and a caller must fall back to moving a length.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Boat.ControlLineLimits.Softplus(System.Single)
member.summary: Numerically-safe softplus ln(1 + e^t); the large-t branch returns t directly to avoid overflow.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Boat.ControlLineLimits.InverseSoftplus(System.Single)
member.summary:
Inverse of : ln(e^t − 1), mirroring its large-t branch. Floored at a small t because the exact inverse runs to −∞ as the force goes to zero — physically "infinitely slack", which is any length past the stopper knot.
Evaluated in double: e^t − 1 cancels catastrophically for the small t a LIGHTLY loaded line produces, and that is the end of the range easing lives at.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Boat.ControlLineLimits.PullFraction(System.Single,System.Single)
member.summary: How far into the crew's pull this tension sits: 0 on a slack line, 1 at the cap. Always 0 for an uncapped line, so an unrigged boat reads as "no load" rather than dividing by infinity into a NaN.
member.param: How hard the crew is pulling, as a fraction of everything they have. This is the TRIGGER: at half, the line behaves as though the cap were half — coming in fast while it is light and slowing to a crawl as it approaches the load that half a pull can hold, rather than being a slower version of the same trip to the same place. A partial pull is a destination.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Boat.ControlLineLimits.PullTarget_N(System.Single)
member.summary: The load a pull of this fraction can hold — where hauling at it stops.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Boat.ControlLineLimits.DistanceRate(System.Single)
member.summary: The fastest the controlled distance may close given of line through the hands: the haul divided by the purchase. A purchase of zero (an unrigged line) is read as a direct pull rather than divided by.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Boat.ControlLineLimits.AtCrewPullMax(System.Single)
member.summary: Is the line at the cap, where hauling can establish no more tension? The margin matches the player input path's, so both stop at the same place.

member.name: T:Sim.Core.Boat.ForceFeed
member.summary: Load-dependent trim feed. The input is modeled as the crew hauling the line; the returned PULL rate is fast on a slack line and eases down a tunable curve to a non-zero floor at max pull. Callers convert pull to controlled-distance rate by dividing by the line's purchase.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Boat.ForceFeed.PullRate(System.Single,System.Single,System.Single,System.Single)
member.summary: Pull rate as a function of the pull fraction (0 = slack, 1 = max pull, clamped): floorRate + (maxRate - floorRate) * (1 - (1+k)*p / (1+k*p)). At p=0 returns maxRate; at p=1 returns floorRate exactly. k=0 is linear; larger k drops faster early then flattens toward the floor. Monotonic, bounded, and never negative for k >= 0 (the caller's responsibility; the curve degenerates for negative k).

member.name: T:Sim.Core.Boat.OuthaulClewSlider
member.summary: One-DOF model of the mainsail clew sliding along the boom under the outhaul. The single DOF is the clew-to-tip distance (the "outhaul distance"): 0 = clew hauled to the boom tip (foot flat), larger = clew eased inboard (foot fuller). The slide is driven by two along-boom forces — the outhaul control-line tension pulling the clew toward the tip (reducing the distance) and the sail's inboard reaction pulling it toward the gooseneck (increasing it) — integrated spring-explicit / damping-implicit, the same scheme as .
member.remarks: The foot outhaul is short, stiff and heavily side-loaded, so it carries far more slide friction than the traveler bridle — a large slideDamping is both physical and what keeps the 1-DOF integration over-damped and stable. Forces are supplied with a one-tick lag (warm-start), matching the rest of the dynamic-leech pipeline.

member.name: P:Sim.Core.Boat.OuthaulClewSlider.ClewToTip_m
member.summary: Clew-to-tip distance (m): the outhaul DOF. 0 = clew at the boom tip (flat foot).

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Boat.OuthaulClewSlider.Update(System.Single,System.Single,System.Single)
member.summary: Advance the clew slide one tick and return the new clew-to-tip distance. Both forces act along the boom: hauls the clew toward the tip (reduces the distance); is the sail's along-boom pull toward the gooseneck (increases it). Supply both with a one-tick lag.

member.name: T:Sim.Core.Boat.Rudder
member.summary: The dynamic rudder blade as a 1-DOF body about the stock axis, the rudder's analogue of . Owns and, like the boom, contributes to via and then integrates the solved joint acceleration via — so I·θ̈ = τ_water + τ_hand is solved TOGETHER with the boat's 6 DOF and the hull feels the blade's reaction. The hand is a stiff PD servo holding the sailor's commanded angle () — "today's rigid feel" is recovered by a high , while a lower one lets the blade sag off the command under stock-torque load (visible weather helm). The hand-feel tunables are so they can be dialled live at the helm.

member.name: P:Sim.Core.Boat.Rudder.HandStiffness_Nm_per_rad
member.summary: PD servo stiffness (N·m per rad of error). High ⇒ a rigid tiller that tracks the commanded angle tightly; low ⇒ a compliant blade that sags under load.

member.name: P:Sim.Core.Boat.Rudder.HandDamping_Nms_per_rad

member.name: T:Sim.Core.Boat.Rudder.StockRotation

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Boat.Rudder.SetStockRotation(System.Numerics.Vector3,System.Numerics.Vector3,System.Single)

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Boat.Rudder.Build(Sim.Core.Appendage.AppendageState@,Sim.Core.Appendage.AppendageInputs@,System.Single)
member.summary: This tick's coupling inputs for , built from the blade's own force-evaluation result. The stiff PD hand τ_hand = k·(cmd − θ) − c·θ̇ is split the way the boom's lines are: the spring goes in the joint torque, while the damping AND the linearised spring dt·k go in , which the solver treats implicitly — that is what keeps a stiff hand on a light blade stable at 5 ms.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Boat.Rudder.HingeTorque_HelmSense(Sim.Core.Appendage.AppendageState@)
member.summary: The hydrodynamic hinge torque in the +helm sense the blade rotates about. StockTorque_Nm is reported about the "up" stock axis, which is the negation of the helm/blade-rotation axis, so it is negated here — an aft-of-pivot CoP then reads as a restoring moment that weathercocks a released blade toward streamline, rather than the self-reinforcing sign the raw stock-axis value would imply.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Boat.Rudder.AssemblySpinTensor_B(Sim.Core.Appendage.AppendageState@)
member.summary: Blade tensor about its own CoM in body axes, plus the tiller rod as a massless flywheel on the stock. Folding the tiller in here (rather than into the joint diagonal alone) is what routes its reaction to the hull — it dominates the joint inertia, so dropping that reaction would be the same class of error the decoupled blade was.

member.name: T:Sim.Core.Boat.Traveler
member.summary: One-DOF model of the mainsheet lower block sliding on a fixed-length bridle (the Laser traveler). See the traveler design (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-03-traveler-design.md).

remarks.para: The block is constrained to the plane through the bail and the two anchors — at frictionless equilibrium the block, anchors and bail are coplanar (the mainsheet bisects the bridle "V"), and we promote that coplanarity to a kinematic constraint. That plane contains the focal axis, so its intersection with the fixed-length spheroid is an ellipse with foci at the anchors. The block rides that ellipse — the single DOF, parametrised by the eccentric angle (bail side, 0..π).

As the boom swings the bail moves and the plane rotates about the anchor-to-anchor axis; the ellipse shape is fixed, so the slide angle carries over untouched. That plane rotation changes neither leg length (no bridle friction) and the slide along the ellipse is integrated with the boom's spring-explicit / damping-implicit scheme. Stable while the tangential stiffness K satisfies K/m·dt² < 4.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Boat.Traveler.#ctor(System.Numerics.Vector3,System.Numerics.Vector3,System.Single,System.Single,System.Single,Sim.Core.Boat.TravelerState)
member.param: Port (+y) bridle anchor, body frame.
Starboard (−y) bridle anchor, body frame.
Total (inextensible) bridle line length. Must exceed the anchor span, otherwise the block has no slack to lift on.
Effective sliding mass (block + the bit of sheet that accelerates with it). Keep large enough that K/m·dt² < 4 for expected tensions.
Viscous slide friction in arc-length space.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Boat.Traveler.WithSpanFraction(System.Numerics.Vector3,System.Numerics.Vector3,System.Single,System.Single,System.Single,Sim.Core.Boat.TravelerState)
member.summary: Build a traveler whose bridle length is expressed as a FRACTION of the anchor span (e.g. 1.05 = 5% longer than the straight-line distance between the anchors). This is the natural way to spec a bridle: the fraction is always ≥ 1 by construction, so the bridle can never be shorter than the span (which would be unphysical and throws in the ctor).
member.param: Bridle length ÷ anchor span. Must be > 1 (a fraction of 1.0 is a taut straight line with no slide; values around 1.03–1.10 give a shallow arc).

member.name: T:Sim.Core.Boat.TrimFeedConfig
member.summary:
Live-tunable trim-feel knobs shared by the control lines (sheet, vang): the pull (tail-haul) speed on a slack line (), the pull speed at max pull (), the falloff steepness (), and and how fast an eased line gives its tension away (). Surfaced as the "Trim" config group; consumes the first three. Rates are PULL speeds — the controlled distance moves at the pull rate divided by the line's purchase.
Shared by the player's input path and the AI trimmer, deliberately: one instance is what makes "the AI is subject to a player's limits" true rather than aspirational.

member.name: T:Sim.Core.Collision.ContactBody
member.summary: One body's input to the : what it is, the convex shapes it presents, and the sphere that bounds all of them for the broad phase. Assembled fresh each tick by the World from a boat's hull or a prop's — detection needs no contest loaded.
member.param: The convex parts this body collides with. One hull today; a boom swinging on its own pose is the reason this is a list rather than a single shape.

How far out this body wants pairs reported even with no touch. A boat carries the umpire's relevance radius because right of way is decided on the approach; a prop carries zero because nothing asks a question about a log until it is hit. A pair is watched at the narrower of the two bands, so one party that only cares about contact drags the pair down to contact — which is what keeps boat-to-prop and prop-to-prop off the 30 m band without the pass knowing what a boat is.
Never moves. Two stationary bodies can never begin to touch, so the pass skips the pair outright.

member.name: T:Sim.Core.Collision.Geometry.Mpr
member.summary: The narrow phase: Minkowski Portal Refinement (XenoCollide). Given two posed convex shapes it answers whether they overlap and, if so, along what normal, by how much, and where — the whole of collision's geometry half.

remarks.para: Chosen over GJK+EPA deliberately. EPA is exact on depth, but it is also where GJK-family implementations habitually break: polytope expansion, horizon-edge extraction, degenerate starting simplices. MPR needs none of that machinery and answers overlap and depth in one pass, so the riskiest code in the module is as small as it can be. Its depth is approximate only in configurations not reachable here.

Everything happens in the Minkowski difference D = A ⊖ B, whose support along a direction is A.Support(dir) − B.Support(−dir). The two shapes overlap exactly when the origin lies inside D, so one construction answers both questions.

member.name: T:Sim.Core.Collision.Geometry.Mpr.Vertex
member.summary: One vertex of the difference, with the witness points on each body that produced it. Kept together because the contact point is a barycentric blend of the witnesses, which is unrecoverable once the difference vertex is separated from where it came from.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Collision.Geometry.Mpr.TryAlongRay(Sim.Core.Collision.Geometry.Mpr.Vertex@,Sim.Core.Collision.Geometry.Mpr.Vertex@,Sim.Core.Collision.Geometry.ContactManifold@)
member.summary: How deep the pair is when the ray runs straight through : the supporting plane there is perpendicular to the ray, so its distance from the origin is the ingress and v1's own witness points bracket the contact. False when that distance is negative — see .

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Collision.Geometry.Mpr.OriginReaches(System.Single)
member.summary: Whether the origin lies on the inside of a supporting plane from it — the test that separates a pair that overlaps from one that merely lines up.
member.remarks:
The difference contains the origin only if every supporting plane has it on the inside, so a negative distance is proof of separation and nothing further need be computed. This is the only place that answers it, because the cheap early exit in cannot: that one tests the FIRST support point against the search ray, which settles it only when the ray happens to run down the separating axis. Off that axis a wide body's support lands on a far corner whose lateral reach dwarfs the gap, the early test passes, and the answer has to come from here.
Clamped at rather than at zero so a pair meeting exactly still reports a contact of zero ingress, which is what the early exit's own strictly-negative test promises. Without this rule the refinement had no way to say "apart" at all: it clamped the negative distance to zero and reported touching, so hulls a hand's breadth clear of each other were separated by the contact response with daylight still between them (#256).

member.summary: Find three difference vertices whose triangle the ray from through the origin passes through. False as soon as a support proves the origin is outside the difference, which is the separation answer arriving free of any depth work.
Push the portal outward until it sits on D's surface. The converged plane's normal is the contact normal and its distance from the origin is the ingress.

member.summary: Blend the portal's witness points by where the ray crosses its triangle, giving a point on each body's surface; the contact acts midway between them.

member.name: T:Sim.Core.Collision.PairwisePass
member.summary: The whole-world pairwise pass (#136): one N² sweep over every body in the water — boats and props alike — emitting each pair worth reporting, flagged with whether the two outlines overlap this instant. Pure and history-free: what a consumer does with a pair is its own business, and the one that judges rules captures what it needs at the tick two hulls meet. See docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-17-boat-boat-pairwise-pass-design.md and docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-11-world-props-design.md.
member.remarks: One nest rather than three, so a further body kind costs a routing arm rather than another loop — and so the two thresholds are stated once. The outputs are typed: a prop cannot appear in the boat-to-boat list, which is what keeps the umpire's input clean by construction.

member.summary: Sweep and fill the three result lists (each cleared first), every pair carrying this instant's outline overlap.

member.name: T:Sim.Core.Collision.Response.ContactEvent
member.summary: One completed contact, summarised: how hard the two bodies were closing when they first touched, the hardest the contact ever pushed, the total impulse it delivered, and how long it lasted. Published when the pair comes apart.
member.remarks: Recorded because none of these numbers can be recovered after the fact — peak force and first-touch closing speed exist only while the contact is happening. The netcode consumes it today, publishing each one as a collision effect. The bet it was recorded FOR is still outstanding: a damage model reads exactly these fields, so when that phase arrives it arrives as a consumer rather than a re-architecture (contact-resolution spec §6).

member.summary: The pair's effective material: two compliant bodies in contact are springs in series, so the softer one governs. That is the mechanism keeping a light body stable against a heavy one's material choice (spec §4) — a mark cannot be handed a hull's stiffness.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Collision.Response.ContactMaterial.Series(System.Single,System.Single)
member.summary: Reciprocal sum, with the two limits that have to behave: a zero-stiffness body carries no force at all (so the pair carries none), and an infinitely stiff one is a wall that leaves the other body's value unchanged. member.remarks: The mass is the lighter body of a pair — it is the one contact accelerates hardest, and it is what actually binds. Spec §4.

member.name: T:Sim.Core.Collision.Response.ContactSolver
member.summary: Turns one touching pair into the loads the two bodies carry next tick. Pure and history-free: the same manifold and the same two parties always give the same answer, so a scripted geometry in a test and a live fleet run identical code.
member.remarks: The force law is a clamped spring-damper (contact-resolution spec §1). The clamp is the whole reason restitution comes out near zero without being a parameter: while the pair closes, spring and damper both resist; as it separates, the damper eats the spring's stored energy rather than returning it, and the clamp stops the force ever going attractive — which is what a naked spring-damper does as it pulls apart, snatching the two bodies back together.

member.summary: One knob writing several objects that must stay identical: every is broadcast to all of them, while reads and the parameter list come from the first.

remarks.para: Not CompositeConfigurable's job. That one merges disjoint parameter sets under a single heading (base wind + shift + puffs); this one fans a single write out across identical ones. member.name: T:Sim.Core.Dynamics.AddedMassComposer
member.summary:
Composes the boat's hull-only diagonal added mass plus every wetted foil's into a single aggregate 6×6 about the aggregate CG. The added-mass analog of . Per the Plan B spec (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-29-added-mass-composer-design.md §5).
Each foil's local-diagonal broadside added mass is rotated into body axes via its LocalToBody and parallel-axis-translated from its centroid to the CG, which generates the rotational added inertia and the translation–rotation coupling: Linear += A; Coupling += −A·[d]×; Angular += −[d]×·A·[d]×, where A = R·diag(PrincipalAddedMass_L)·Rᵀ and d = Centroid_B − cg_B. The hull diagonal is already about the CG and is added directly.

member.name: T:Sim.Core.Dynamics.ArticulatedSolver
member.summary:
Monolithic minimal-coordinate (composite-rigid-body) solve for the boat (6 DOF) coupled to its articulated children: the boom (2 hinge DOF) and the rudder blade (1 stock DOF). Assembles the generalized mass matrix as blocks A (boat 6×6), B (coupling 6×n) and D (joint n×n), and eliminates the joint block by Schur complement so the boat keeps going through SpatialInertia.Solve. Pure/stateless.
The boom and the rudder are independent children of the same base — neither hinges off the other — so their D block is block-diagonal. They are NOT independent in the eliminated system: the Schur complement's off-diagonal −B_boomᵀA⁻¹B_rud is the hull recoil each child feels from the other, and dropping it violates Newton's third law and leaks momentum. Hence one joint solve over all active DOFs, not a scalar solve per child.

member.name: F:Sim.Core.Dynamics.ArticulatedSolver.MaxJoints
member.summary: Joint slots, in the order they occupy columns of the joint system.

Schur-eliminate the boat block and solve the joint system S·q̈ = r, where S = D − BᵀA⁻¹B and r = τ_joint − BᵀA⁻¹f_boat. Returns the boat's body-frame acceleration about the composite CG, aInvRhs − Σᵢ q̈ᵢ·A⁻¹Bᵢ, and writes q̈ into .

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Dynamics.ArticulatedSolver.SolveSymmetric(System.Span{System.Single},System.Span{System.Single},System.Span{System.Single},System.Int32)
M:Sim.Core.Dynamics.ArticulatedSolver.ChildInertiaAboutCG(System.Single,System.Numerics.Vector3,Sim.Core.Dynamics.Matrix3x3@,System.Numerics.Vector3)
member.summary: One articulated child's spatial inertia about the composite CG. Sign convention: Coupling stores the upper-right block −m[c]×. SpatialInertia.Multiply uses Coupling.Transpose() for the lower-left block, giving the standard rigid-body spatial inertia [[m·I, −m[c]×],[m[c]×, Ic + m(|c|²I − c⊗c)]]. The angular block uses the closed form m(|c|²I − c⊗c), which equals −m[c]×[c]×, consistent with AddedMassComposer's −[d]×A[d]× shifted-inertia pattern.

Velocity-product bias of the boom branch via a 2-body RNEA pass at zero acceleration, gravity off. The gooseneck is a UNIVERSAL joint whose pitch axis rides on the yaw angle (PitchAxis_B = (−sinψ,−cosψ,0)), so it must be treated as a chain, not a lumped 2-DOF joint: each joint's Coriolis term uses the spatial velocity AT that joint. Using the full boom velocity for BOTH terms drops the yaw↔pitch cross term ψ̇θ̇·crm(Φpitch)·Φyaw — the pitch axis rotating with yaw — and breaks momentum conservation whenever both DOFs move. The gyroscopic force crf still uses the boom's full velocity.

member.name: T:Sim.Core.Dynamics.ComponentAddedMass
member.summary: Hydrodynamic added-mass contribution of a single underwater foil, published per tick on its . Mirrors : is the foil's added mass as a local diagonal — for a thin foil the only significant term is the broadside (section-normal) translational added mass, placed on the local-y axis as (0, A_n, 0). member.name: T:Sim.Core.Dynamics.ComponentInertia
member.summary: Local-frame inertia contribution of a single rigid component (hull, mast, sail, daggerboard, rudder, crew, boom, …). Composed into the boat-level aggregate by per design-doc §20.2.

remarks.para: The principal-inertia diagonal is in the component's own local frame, about the component's own centre of mass. The composition step (§20.4) rotates it into body frame via the component's LocalToBody quaternion and then parallel-axis-translates from the component CoM to the boat-body origin.

V1 convention for : the field carries the CoM position in body frame directly. Every Laser v1 component has a local frame whose origin coincides with the component's body-frame placement point, with LocalToBody at most rotating the principal axes about that point. Storing the body-frame position avoids the impedance mismatch with quaternions (which have no translation) and matches what the models already compute for force placement. Future tilted components ride the same composer code path with non-identity LocalToBody for the tensor rotation.

V1 stores only the diagonal of the local-frame inertia tensor. Every Laser component is principal-axis-aligned in its own local frame by construction (rods along their length, plates with one short axis, hull with longitudinal symmetry). The §20.11 forward-compat note explains when to lift this to a full .

T:Sim.Core.Dynamics.ForceAggregator
member.summary: Accumulates a stream of contributions into a net force and net torque about a chosen reference point in world frame (typically the hull CG). Reset and reused every tick.
member.remarks:
Mathematically: net torque about reference point P from a force F applied at point r is τ = (r − P) × F. The accumulator runs that for every contribution and sums.
The reference point may move tick-to-tick (CG shifts when crew moves), but within a single tick it is fixed — set once in the constructor or via , then all calls accumulate against that one point.

member.name: T:Sim.Core.Dynamics.InertiaComposer
member.summary: Composes per-component contributions (hull, mast, sails, appendages, crew, boom) into a single boat-aggregate in body frame about the aggregate CG. Per design-doc §20.4. Pure function — runs once per tick before the integrator consumes the result.

Compose the boat-aggregate inertial properties from one tick's per-component state records. The boom is folded in as a point mass per §20.5 — its own rotational inertia stays inside Boom.Update's 2-DOF integrator and must not double-count in the boat aggregate (legacy path; when BoomCoupling is ON, ArticulatedSolver adds the boom's spin tensor to the composite block instead — InertiaComposer still contributes the boom point mass for the CG/parallel-axis term in both paths).
member.param: Per-sail state records. Sail mass is a single point at the sail-local centroid; rotates the offset into body frame each tick (so the mainsail's mass swings with the boom).

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Dynamics.RigidBodyDynamics.AccelerationFromForces(System.Numerics.Vector3,System.Numerics.Vector3,Sim.Core.Dynamics.RigidBodyProperties@,System.Numerics.Quaternion,System.Numerics.Vector3,System.Numerics.Vector3)
member.summary: Solve for accelerations given net force/torque, mass/inertia, and the body-frame linear added mass. The linear solve divides per axis in the body frame (a_B = R⁻¹F ⨸ (m + mₐ), rotated back); rotational added mass is expected to be folded into 's inertia tensor by the caller. A zero added-mass vector takes an exact F/m fast path, so legacy callers are bit-for-bit unchanged.
member.param: Body angular velocity in world frame; needed for the gyroscopic Euler term once the inertia tensor has off-diagonal entries. Pass for a pure static moment balance.
Body-frame translational added mass per axis (kg). Zero ⇒ exact F/m.
member.remarks: Linear: per-axis a_B = R⁻¹F / (m + mₐ), rotated to world (exact F/m when mₐ = 0). Angular: solves Euler's equation in body frame I·α_B = τ_B − ω_B × (I·ω_B), then α_W = R·α_B.

member.summary: Added-mass entries at or below this magnitude are treated as zero for the fast-path decision. Below the single-precision noise floor for physical added-mass values (O(1)–O(1e3) kg / kg·m²), so any genuine entry exceeds it.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Dynamics.RigidBodyDynamics.SolveEffectiveMass(System.Numerics.Vector3,System.Numerics.Vector3,Sim.Core.Dynamics.RigidBodyProperties@,System.Numerics.Quaternion,System.Numerics.Vector3,Sim.Core.Dynamics.SpatialInertia@)
member.summary: Always-matrix coupled solve: assemble the effective inertia M_eff = rigid + added (a ), build the body-frame load, and solve M_eff·a = b for the 6-DOF acceleration. The gyroscopic term uses the EFFECTIVE angular block, preserving the Stage-1 behaviour (added-mass Coriolis deferred). No fast-path branch — this is the method the equivalence test targets. The assembled M_eff = rigid + must be symmetric positive-definite; otherwise throws from a singular block.

member.name: T:Sim.Core.Dynamics.SpatialInertia
member.summary: A 6×6 symmetric spatial-inertia matrix — linear mass + rotational inertia + their coupling. The standard term from spatial-vector algebra (robotics) and Fossen's marine-craft "inertia matrix". One type for the rigid-body inertia, the added mass, and the effective inertia; instances are named by role. Stored as three blocks — the full matrix is [[Linear, Coupling], [Couplingᵀ, Angular]], the lower-left being the transpose of (symmetry). Physical instances are symmetric positive-definite; symmetry and positive-definiteness are the caller's responsibility — no validation is performed.

member.summary: Translation–translation block (A).

member.name: F:Sim.Core.Dynamics.SpatialInertia.Coupling
member.summary: Translation–rotation block (B); the lower-left block is its transpose.

member.summary: Rotation–rotation block (D).

member.summary: Rigid-body inertia about the CG: m·I on translation, the inertia tensor on rotation.

member.summary: The diagonals of the linear and angular blocks (per-axis values).

member.summary: True if any coupling-block entry exceeds in magnitude.

member.summary: True if the matrix is (near-)diagonal: no coupling block AND no off-diagonal entries in the linear or angular blocks (every off-diagonal ≤ ). When true the 6×6 solve degenerates to per-axis division, so the diagonals fully describe the matrix.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Dynamics.SpatialInertia.Multiply(System.Numerics.Vector3,System.Numerics.Vector3)
member.summary: Apply the matrix to a 6-vector (xLin, xAng): returns M·x.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Dynamics.SpatialInertia.Solve(System.Numerics.Vector3,System.Numerics.Vector3)
member.summary: Solve M·x = b for x, given b = (bLin, bAng). Symmetric block (Schur-complement) solve using the 3×3 blocks; valid for SPD M (the linear block and the Schur complement are invertible). x_ang = (D − Bᵀ A⁻¹ B)⁻¹ (b_ang − Bᵀ A⁻¹ b_lin); x_lin = A⁻¹ (b_lin − B x_ang). Throws (from ) if the linear block or the Schur complement is singular — callers must ensure M is SPD.

member.name: T:Sim.Core.Dynamics.SymmetricEigen
member.summary: Cyclic Jacobi eigensolver for a real symmetric 3×3 matrix. Introduced for §20 inertia derivation: a foil's geometric inertia tensor (computed about its volume centroid by ) carries small products of inertia from taper and sweep, but stores only a diagonal principal inertia plus a LocalToBody rotation. This factors the symmetric tensor into eigenvalues (principal inertias) and orthonormal eigenvectors (principal axes) so the composer can reconstruct it via R·diag·Rᵀ.
member.remarks: Jacobi is the right tool for tiny symmetric matrices: unconditionally convergent, no pivoting, deterministic, and accurate even for near-degenerate (near-symmetric foil) tensors. Internals run in double for robustness; results are returned as float.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Dynamics.SymmetricEigen.Solve(Sim.Core.Dynamics.Matrix3x3)
member.summary: Diagonalize a symmetric 3×3. Returns the eigenvalues and an orthonormal eigenvector matrix whose columns are the unit eigenvectors (so Eigenvectors · diag(Eigenvalues) · Eigenvectorsᵀ reconstructs the input). Eigenvalue Eigenvalues[k] pairs with the k-th column. The off-diagonal halves of the input are averaged, so a slightly non-symmetric matrix is treated as its symmetric part.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Dynamics.SymmetricEigen.RotateColumns(System.Double@,System.Double@,System.Double,System.Double)
member.summary: Rotate a pair of matrix entries (one row across columns p,q) by the Jacobi angle: (xp, xq) ← (c·xp − s·xq, s·xp + c·xq).

member.summary:
The one height "the true wind" is reported at, for every consumer that wants the wind rather than the wind at some particular point of the boat — observation, telemetry, course geometry. Near masthead (a Laser's is 5.81 m), so it reads the breeze the rig is working in rather than the one scraping the deck.
Distinct from LayeredWindField's RefHeight config, which is where the shear profile's RefSpeed is defined (10 m, the meteorological standard). That one parameterises the profile; this one samples it.

member.name: F:Sim.Core.Environment.IWindField.DriftReferenceHeight_m
member.summary:
The one height a disturbance layer reads the mean wind at to set the velocity its frozen pattern is advected with. Masthead-ish and pattern-wide — the whole field rides one velocity, not a per-sample one, so this is a property of the layer rather than of the point being sampled.
Shared so the layers cannot disagree: fronts and puffs riding different velocities would drift apart over a run, and nothing would say why.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Environment.IWindField.Velocity(System.Numerics.Vector3,System.Single)
member.summary: Wind velocity vector at world position and time . Steady implementations ignore ; stochastic implementations use it to drive temporal variation.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Environment.IWindField.TrueWind(System.Numerics.Vector2,System.Single)
member.summary:
The true wind over at time — sampled at the shared , so every consumer reports the same wind for the same place.
Takes a horizontal position precisely because the height is not the caller's to choose. Sampling "the" true wind at a boat's own z is what made it depend on where the hull happened to be riding: at the hull origin the sample sits on the waterline, and in a seaway it drops below z = 0, where the profile floors to zero wind and the bearing of a zero vector is undefined. Callers that genuinely want the wind at a specific point of the boat — a sail panel, the mast — still call with that point.

member.name: T:Sim.Core.Geometry.BoundingSphere

Sibling capsule/box fitters can follow the same shape when elongated parts (foils, boom) need a tighter volume. See docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-24-any-part-crossing-design.md §3.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Geometry.BoundingSphere.Fit(System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList{System.Numerics.Vector3})
member.summary: Ritter's approximate-minimal bounding sphere. O(n), encloses every point.

member.name: T:Sim.Core.Geometry.ConvexShape
member.summary: A convex collision shape in its body's own frame: a set of points and a sweep radius. Its whole surface is one support query, which is all the narrow phase ever asks of it.

remarks.para: The points need no convex hull. argmax over a cloud returns exactly the support point of that cloud's convex hull — an interior point can never win a maximum — so a raw mesh vertex list is its hull as far as anything here is concerned. A hull's cockpit fills implicitly, which is correct: you cannot strike another boat with the inside of your own cockpit.

Where the points came from is not this type's business. Decimated, hand-authored, or lifted off the render mesh — nothing downstream can tell, and nothing may ask. The fidelity policy is decided once at composition so it stays swappable without touching an algorithm.

member.name: P:Sim.Core.Geometry.ConvexShape.SweepRadius_m
member.summary: How far the point set is inflated — the Minkowski sum with a ball of this radius. Zero for anything backed by a mesh; a genuinely round shape is one point plus its radius.

member.name: P:Sim.Core.Geometry.ConvexShape.Bounds_B
member.summary: Bounding sphere over this shape's own points, grown by .

member.name: P:Sim.Core.Geometry.ConvexShape.PointCount
member.summary: How many points back this shape. For diagnostics and cost budgeting only — no behaviour may branch on it, or the "where the points came from" seam has leaked.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Geometry.ConvexShape.Support(System.Numerics.Vector3)
member.summary: The farthest this shape reaches along , in body frame.
member.remarks: A zero direction has no farthest point and normalize is undefined there, so it resolves to one fixed axis. The rule lives here rather than in each caller because the direction genuinely does collapse — the narrow phase seeds from the vector between two bodies, which is zero for coincident centres — and a NaN escaping into a body's velocity is unrecoverable.

member.name: T:Sim.Core.Geometry.HullShape
member.summary: A hull's collision geometry in the body frame, captured once at composition. This is the shape — where it currently is belongs to the projection.

member.name: P:Sim.Core.Geometry.HullShape.BowX_m
member.summary: Body-frame x of the foremost point of the hull; the aftmost. Reported as the two ends rather than as a length, because where they sit relative to any given reference point is the question, and a length has already thrown that away.
member.remarks: From , which is the narrow phase's own support function and already accounts for the sweep radius, rather than from the bounding sphere — which is fitted to the diagonal and would report a hull longer than it is.

member.name: P:Sim.Core.Geometry.HullShape.Length_m
member.summary: Length overall (m) — the hull's fore-aft extent. Derived from the two ends rather than stored, so it cannot drift from them.

member.name: P:Sim.Core.Geometry.HullShape.Beam_m
member.summary: Beam (m) — the hull's athwartships extent, the sibling of and taken from the same support queries already makes.

member.name: P:Sim.Core.Geometry.HullShape.Center_B
member.summary: Body-frame centre of the hull's own extents — the point that means "where this boat is". Midway between her ends on each axis, so a hull symmetric about her centreline has it on that centreline whatever her plan shape.
member.remarks: Deliberately NOT 's centre, which is a bounding volume's centre and answers a different question. Ritter seeds from an approximate diameter, and for a hull that diameter runs corner to opposite corner — so the centre lands off the plane of symmetry: 22 cm to port on the shipped hull, against a 68 cm half-beam. That is harmless for a broad phase, which only needs the sphere to enclose, and wrong for anything comparing two boats athwartships, which is what reading it as the boat's position made rule 11 do.

member.name: P:Sim.Core.Geometry.HullShape.Collision
member.summary: What the narrow phase tests: the hull as a convex shape, correct at any attitude.

member.name: P:Sim.Core.Geometry.HullShape.Sphere_B
member.summary: Broad-phase volume, taken from the collision shape's own points rather than any other geometry — a shape reaching past the sphere that bounds it is a pair the sweep silently drops.

member.name: T:Sim.Core.Geometry.NacaProfile
member.summary: The NACA 4-digit symmetric thickness law — pure geometry, shared by the foil geometry integrals ( volume / inertia), the model-side aero correlations (Sim.Models.Util.NacaSection), and the renderer's foil mesh builder. Lives in Sim.Core so all three can share one source of truth for the section shape.
member.remarks: The closed-trailing-edge coefficients (a₄ = 0.1036, vs the standard open-TE 0.1015) are used so the section closes cleanly at the trailing edge — matching the mesh the renderer draws.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Geometry.NacaProfile.HalfThickness(System.Single)
member.summary: Half-thickness of the section as a fraction of chord, for a UNIT thickness ratio, at chord fraction ∈ [0,1] (0 = leading edge, 1 = trailing edge). The actual half-thickness in metres is HalfThickness(u) · (t/c) · chord, and the full local thickness is twice that.

member.name: F:Sim.Core.Geometry.NacaProfile.AreaCoefficient
member.summary: Section area coefficient K = ∫₀¹ 2·HalfThickness(u) du, so a section of local chord c and thickness ratio t/c has cross-sectional area c² · (t/c) · K. Evaluated in closed form from the coefficients above: K = 2·5·(a0·⅔ + a1·½ + a2·⅓ + a3·¼ + a4·⅕) ≈ 0.68088.

member.name: T:Sim.Core.Geometry.Planform
member.summary: Whether two posed shapes' plan-view footprints meet — their shadows on the water, height discarded.

remarks.para: It costs no new data, because a support function projects. For a convex body, the footprint's support in a horizontal direction is exactly the XY part of the 3D support in that direction: the point that reaches furthest that way reaches furthest in the shadow too, whatever its height. So already IS the footprint's support function, and nothing is flattened, cached or stored. That matters beyond convenience — a second notion of where a hull is is the trap c0eb0d0 deleted when it removed the flattened deck-edge outline. It holds for a swept shape too: the sweep offsets the support point along a horizontal unit direction, which is the same disc the footprint of a swept body is inflated by.

Touching counts as meeting. Two footprints exactly end to end are not disjoint, which is the answer the overlap definition needs: a boat whose bow has just arrived at another's transom has not come alongside her.
2D GJK over the Minkowski difference: the two footprints intersect exactly when that difference contains the origin. Iterative and exact for convex shapes, with no tolerance to tune.

member.name: F:Sim.Core.Geometry.Planform.MaxIterations
member.summary: Far more than a hull needs — GJK on a convex polygon converges in a handful of folds, and exhausting this means the simplex is cycling on float ties rather than closing in.

member.name: F:Sim.Core.Geometry.Planform.Collinear
member.summary: Sine of the angle below which two vectors count as collinear. Relative, because the quantity it bounds scales with both their lengths.

member.name: F:Sim.Core.Geometry.Planform.Degenerate
member.summary: Below this a direction has no direction left to give, and the two shapes are as good as on top of each other.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Geometry.Planform.MinkowskiSupport(Sim.Core.Geometry.PosedShape@,Sim.Core.Geometry.PosedShape@,System.Numerics.Vector2)
member.summary: How far the Minkowski difference of the two footprints reaches along .

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Geometry.Planform.FootprintSupport(Sim.Core.Geometry.PosedShape@,System.Numerics.Vector2)
member.summary: The footprint's support point — the 3D support along the same direction, flattened. See the class remarks for why that is exact rather than an approximation.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Geometry.Planform.Fold(System.Span{System.Numerics.Vector2},System.Int32@,System.Numerics.Vector2@)
member.summary: Fold the newest point into the simplex: true once it encloses the origin, otherwise the simplex is cut back to the feature facing the origin and is left pointing from that feature toward it.
member.remarks: The newest point is always kept, and always ends up last — every fold reads it from count - 1, so a reduction that leaves it anywhere else silently feeds the next iteration a degenerate simplex, which then reports every pair as meeting.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Geometry.Planform.OriginIsOnTheEdge(System.Numerics.Vector2,System.Numerics.Vector2,System.Numerics.Vector2@)
member.summary: Aim from the segment at the origin. True when the two are collinear, which here means the origin lies ON the segment — the support test that admitted this point has already ruled out its being beyond either end.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Geometry.Planform.Perpendicular(System.Numerics.Vector2,System.Single)
member.summary: The perpendicular to on the side names — the 2D triple product, which is how GJK turns "which way is the origin" into a direction. Only its direction is ever read, so the length it carries does not matter.

member.name: T:Sim.Core.Geometry.VectorMath
member.summary: Pure vector primitives shared across the layers — no model state, no units, just in and out. Lives in Sim.Core so the rig solvers, the mesh builders and their tests all call one implementation instead of each hand-rolling their own.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Geometry.VectorMath.RotateAboutAxis(System.Numerics.Vector3,System.Numerics.Vector3,System.Single)
member.summary: Rotate about by (Rodrigues' formula, right-handed). The axis must be a unit vector — this does not normalise it, so a non-unit axis scales the result.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Geometry.VectorMath.NormalizeOr(System.Numerics.Vector3,System.Numerics.Vector3)
member.summary: Unit vector along , or when is too short for its direction to mean anything (see ).

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Geometry.VectorMath.InterpolateDirection(System.Numerics.Vector3,System.Numerics.Vector3,System.Single)
member.summary: Interpolate between two directions along the arc between them, so the result keeps unit length and turns at a constant rate. A straight line between two directions cuts through the sphere rather than following it — it sags short of unit length in the middle, worst where the directions are furthest apart.
member.remarks: Near-parallel directions have almost no arc to follow, so the straight line is both indistinguishable from it and better conditioned; antiparallel directions have no unique arc at all, and turn through an arbitrary but deterministic one.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Geometry.VectorMath.PerpendicularTo(System.Numerics.Vector3,System.Numerics.Vector3)
member.summary: Unit vector perpendicular to and as close to as possible — with its component along the axis removed. A caller wanting the opposite negates the result; a caller wanting a particular one of the infinitely many perpendiculars says which through .
member.remarks: A parallel to the axis expresses no preference — none of it survives the projection — so an arbitrary but deterministic perpendicular comes back instead. must be a unit vector, or the projection is not one.

member.name: T:Sim.Core.Precision
member.summary: The sim's float-precision gates — the thresholds below which a quantity is indistinguishable from zero and its direction is rounding error rather than data. One value, shared, so a degenerate segment is judged degenerate the same way everywhere.
member.remarks: These are not domain thresholds. A cutoff that encodes a physical or modelling decision — when two directions count as parallel, how close a boat must be to a mark, a test's tolerance — is a property of that decision and belongs with it, not here. Only "is this float zero yet?" belongs in this type.

member.name: F:Sim.Core.Precision.NearZero

member.name: T:Sim.Core.Racing.ContactAt
member.summary: A latched touch as an is handed it: when the hulls met, this pair's overlap as it stood THEN, and both boats as they stood then (spec §3.5, #335).

remarks.para: The four travel together because they are one question — what was true at the touch — and answering part of it is worse than answering none: rule 12 turns entirely on the overlap, so a snapshot pair read at the touch and an overlap read at the drain would still swap who keeps clear.

The snapshots ride here rather than being looked up. They used to come from each party's window, which floors to the newest 4 Hz sample at or before the touch — so a verdict was read from a fleet state up to 250 ms older than the contact, and an overlap established inside that window was invisible. Both halves agreed with each other while describing a moment that was not the contact, which is why nothing downstream could notice. Captured at the touching tick instead, by the one thing that runs at tick rate and holds the fleet's RRS state (#335).
is the lower-id boat, — the order reads its two windows in.

member.name: T:Sim.Core.Racing.RawFeature
member.summary: A raw, pre-derivation feature: a kind plus the buoy ids it references. Segment features (Start/Finish/Gate) name two buoys, ordered so the port-rounding buoy is first and the plane normal is 90° right of first→second: start / windward gate = left→right, leeward gate = right→left (start = pin→boat). A Mark names one buoy; its is an optional override — null means "use the course's default direction".

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Racing.RoundingBuoy.#ctor(System.Numerics.Vector2,System.Nullable{Sim.Core.Racing.Rounding})

member.name: T:Sim.Core.Racing.CourseFeature
member.summary: One course feature with its derived scoring s and the counter target that completes it (1 for Start/Finish, 2 for Mark/Gate). Scoring is a pure sum of its lines' per-tick crossings; the owning holds the running counter. See spec §7.

member.name: P:Sim.Core.Racing.CourseFeature.Roles
member.summary: Line roles for rendering (same order as ): which to draw as a segment wall vs. a ray wall, and whether it is the entry. Index-aligned.

member.name: P:Sim.Core.Racing.CourseFeature.Extensions
member.summary: A starting line's two extensions, running outward from its ends — empty for every other feature. Course geometry, so the course lays them once and the guidance walls can draw them; but not scoring lines, and deliberately not reachable from .
member.remarks:
A separate collection rather than a role inside , because these are not the feature's to advance. Rule 30.1 needs a tick's crossing on them before the tracker is asked whether she may start, so their owner advances them; a stateful line advanced in two places consumes the crossing twice, and whichever caller ran second would see nothing.
Keeping them out of shuts the two ways that went wrong before: cannot reach them to double-advance, cannot re-arm them behind their owner's back, and the next line role added cannot opt into scoring by forgetting to exclude itself. It does not make single ownership impossible to break -- is public and this list is reachable from anything holding the feature, the renderer included. Advancing one of these from anywhere but its owner consumes the crossing rule 30.1 is waiting for.

member.name: P:Sim.Core.Racing.CourseFeature.Buoys
member.summary: The feature's buoys with their rounding — what a tactician reads: one for a Mark, two (port-first) for a Gate, or the two ordered ends (no rounding) for a start / finish line. Positions are rest-frame.

member.name: T:Sim.Core.Racing.CourseLegs
member.summary: The course measured as distance to sail: each leg's rhumb length, and how far a boat part-way round still owes. Fixed geometry — built once with the course and never refreshed, because the marks do not move.
member.remarks: Course-referenced, not wind-referenced, and the choice matters. Ladder rungs — the projection onto the wind axis — are how a sailor reads who is ahead on a beat, and they track a shift, which this does not. But they go degenerate on a leg square to the wind (an offset mark spans no rungs, so every boat on it reads as tied), and they do not answer the question a gap quoted in metres asks: two boats on the same rung, one on the layline and one dead downwind of the mark, have very different distances left to sail. Shift-awareness belongs in a tactical readout, not in the scoreboard's number.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Racing.CourseLegs.RemainingFrom(System.Numerics.Vector2,System.Int32)
member.summary: Distance still to sail from with feature the one being sailed to: a straight line to that feature, plus the rhumb length of every leg after it. Zero when there is no active feature.
member.remarks: Straight-line to the mark rather than a projection onto the leg, so a boat wide of the rhumb line owes the distance it must really sail rather than reading as level with a boat on the line. That also makes it continuous across a rounding: the "0 m to this mark, plus the next leg" a boat owes at the mark is the same number as the "next leg's full length" it owes once the rounding advances the index.

member.name: T:Sim.Core.Racing.CourseRegistry
member.summary: Resolves a course id to the stock course document it names. Courses are class-standard shipped resources that ride by id rather than as content (the SessionConfig design's "referenced by id" rule), so a remote client — or a C caller with 32 bytes to spend — reproduces one locally instead of receiving it.

remarks.para: The ids are hand-written words rather than file names or ordinals: they are typed into a SimSessionDesc.course_id[32] by hand, so they have to be short, spellable and stable. A file name would tie the wire to the asset tree, and an ordinal would silently re-point every caller the day a fifth course is inserted in the middle.

An unknown id is an error, never open water. "No course" is said by naming no course at all (an empty course_id, a null Sim.World.Setup.SessionConfig.Race); a name nobody can resolve is a caller's mistake, and answering it with an empty sea is issue #330 — a session that reported success and had no race in it.

A table rather than a registry type, for the reason BoatClassRegistry gives: this is four shipped documents, and a fifth adds one row. is the one home for that list — what a menu offers and what a session may name are the same set, read from here by both.

member.name: P:Sim.Core.Racing.CourseRegistry.Ids
member.summary: The stock course ids, in menu order — what a caller may name, so a consumer can offer the list rather than guess at it.
member.remarks: Wrapped rather than handed out as the array: this is one process-wide list, and an IReadOnlyList over a bare array casts back to a writable one.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Racing.CourseRegistry.Json(System.String)
member.summary: The course document names, ready for . Parsing needs the wind the caller places it in, so what is held here is the text, not a .
member.exception: The id names no stock course. Deliberately loud: see the class remarks.

member.name: T:Sim.Core.Racing.DeemedOverlaps
member.summary: Which boats are overlapped once RRS's transitive clause is applied — "they are also overlapped when a boat between them overlaps both".

remarks.para: Betweenness is half the rule, and it is the half that is easy to drop. This began as the connected components of the directly-overlapped graph, on the reasoning that overlap is symmetric so closing it transitively is exactly finding components. That is sound only while the relation behaves like intervals on one axis, and it does not: the line-abeam test measures along each boat's OWN fore axis and has no lateral bound, so two boats abeam are overlapped however far apart they are. A boat 27 m away on a near-perpendicular heading therefore read as overlapped with two others and bridged them, deeming a boat 4.7 m clear astern to be overlapped.

This does not close that hole, and must not be read as having closed it. The test below bounds where the middle boat sits ALONG the line joining the two, and not at all how far she sits off it — so a boat 50 m abeam of the pair, at a fore-and-aft station between them, still bridges them. The root cause is the pairwise relation being unbounded athwartships (#344); until that is settled, this removes one route to the absurdity rather than the absurdity. What it does buy is faithfulness: the rule says between, and components never asked.

Iterated to a fixed point, not applied once. Read literally the clause is one hop, which would leave a line of four boats — each overlapping only her neighbour — with the ends clear of each other. Applying it repeatedly is what makes a whole line overlapped, and each step still has a real boat genuinely between the pair it joins.

The cost is O(n³) per pass and at most one pass per pair added, which is fine for the fleets this races (single digits) and would not be for a hundred boats. It is bounded by the fleet, not by the tick rate: this runs once per 4 Hz umpire sample.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Racing.DeemedOverlaps.Of(System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList{System.ValueTuple{Sim.Core.BoatId,Sim.Core.Racing.RrsSnapshot}},System.Collections.Generic.HashSet{System.ValueTuple{Sim.Core.BoatId,Sim.Core.BoatId}})
member.summary: Close the directly-overlapped pairs under the transitive clause. Indices are into , which is what the caller already iterates by.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Racing.DeemedOverlaps.Between(System.Numerics.Vector2,System.Numerics.Vector2,System.Numerics.Vector2)
member.summary: Whether lies between and — her position projected onto the line joining them, and required to land on the segment rather than off either end.
member.remarks: Positions rather than hulls: "between" is about where she is, and a hull test would make the answer turn on the last centimetre of a transom at the exact moment two boats are level. Coincident endpoints have no segment and so nothing can be between them — which is the honest answer, and it is also unreachable, since two boats in the same place are directly overlapped and never reach this.

member.name: T:Sim.Core.Racing.Encounter
member.summary: One pair's engagement — the stateful heart of the umpire (spec §3.4/§3.5). It is created unconditionally for any candidate pair and stepped each 4 Hz sample over the two parties' history windows. It reconciles the rule(s) in force into s and resolves each sample one of four ways: contact → foul; the right-of-way boat forced to maneuver → foul; the pair separated and settled → clean close; roles changed → an application closes, the encounter goes on. P1 implements rule 10 only, but the two-level Encounter/RuleApplication shape is the seam that lets 11/12/13 and Sections B/C land as additions.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Racing.Encounter.Step(Sim.Core.Racing.PartyWindow,Sim.Core.Racing.PartyWindow,System.Nullable{Sim.Core.Racing.ContactAt},Sim.Core.Racing.OverlapRelation,System.Single)
member.param: This pair's overlap as the fleet-level resolver settled it this sample. Passed in for the same reason is: both are facts about the pair that something outside it establishes, and an encounter that derived its own would be re-deriving — with no way to see the boat between two others that overlaps both.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Racing.Encounter.AtTheTouch(Sim.Core.Racing.ContactAt@)
member.summary: Who had to keep clear when the hulls met, rather than when the touch was drained (spec §3.5), together with what that verdict was read from.

remarks.para: Everything comes off the touch itself now. The relation and both snapshots were captured at the touching tick and travel on , so this no longer walks the 4 Hz windows back to it. It used to, and both halves floored to the newest sample at or before — agreeing with each other while describing a fleet state up to 250 ms older than the contact. An overlap established inside that window was invisible, which called rule 12 where rule 11 applied and generally on the wrong boat (#335).

The verdict and the evidence come back from one call because they are one computation. Deriving them separately is how they would come to disagree, and a record of a verdict that does not match the verdict is worse than no record.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Racing.Encounter.BothAt(Sim.Core.Racing.PartyWindow,Sim.Core.Racing.PartyWindow,System.Single,Sim.Core.Racing.RrsSnapshot@,Sim.Core.Racing.RrsSnapshot@)
member.summary: Both parties as they stood at one instant, or false if either window cannot reach it. Both or neither: a verdict or a projection built from one boat's history and the other's default snapshot is a well-formed answer about a moment that never happened.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Racing.Encounter.Parted(Sim.Core.Racing.RrsSnapshot@,Sim.Core.Racing.RrsSnapshot@)
member.summary: The pair is done with each other: out of every relevance gate, and neither mid-maneuver. The one condition that ends an encounter, whether it was ever judged or not.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Racing.Encounter.Settled(Sim.Core.Racing.RrsSnapshot@,Sim.Core.Racing.RrsSnapshot@)
member.summary: Neither boat is mid-manoeuvre. Deliberately NOT also "and no longer overlapped", which the P1 note here anticipated: overlap is a fore-and-aft test with no lateral bound, so two boats sailing parallel up the beat a hundred metres apart are overlapped for as long as they are abeam. Requiring it to break would keep their encounter open the whole leg, and every other pair like them — the relevance gates are what bound an engagement in space, and they already do.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Racing.Encounter.RightOfWayBoatForcedToManeuver(Sim.Core.Racing.PartyWindow,Sim.Core.Racing.PartyWindow,Sim.Core.Racing.Party,System.Single)
member.summary: The necessity walk-back (spec §3.5): if the right-of-way boat began a course change, project both boats forward from the pre-maneuver sample un-maneuvered. A projected closest approach inside the contact margin means the maneuver was forced — a foul on the keep-clear boat. Otherwise she was sailing her own race.

member.name: T:Sim.Core.Racing.IRelevanceGate

member.name: T:Sim.Core.Racing.JudgedPair
member.summary: One pair the umpire is asked to judge this sample, and the touch it carries — null for a pair that has not met since the last drain.

remarks.para: The umpire's own input shape, rather than NearPair straight off the collision pass. The pass is geometry and knows nothing of rules; what the umpire needs beside a pair is what was TRUE at the touch (), which only a caller holding RRS state can assemble. Keeping that on this side of the seam is what stops an overlap relation leaking into a collision type.
Near-set membership still comes from the pass — a pair reaches here because the broad phase put it here — so this adds the rules half without re-deriving the geometry half.
