member.name: T:Sim.Core.Racing.OverlapGeometry
member.summary: The instantaneous line-abeam test between two boats (spec §3.3). RRS defines it from the hulls: a boat is clear astern when her hull is behind a line abeam from the aftmost point of the other's hull, the other is then clear ahead, and they overlap when neither is clear astern. Both ends are read off the hulls themselves, by support query.
member.remarks: Pure and stateless, which is what keeps it separate from : this answers "are they overlapped in this instant", and the rule asks a question no instant can answer — an overlap that has been established stands until it is broken, only a crossing while the planforms are apart establishes one at all, and a boat between two others overlaps them to each other. Those need history, history again, and the whole fleet.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Racing.OverlapGeometry.Between(System.Single,System.Single)
member.summary: The same test read off already taken, for a caller that needs more than one answer from them — the relation, the separation and which boat is further behind are all functions of these two numbers, and taking them costs four support queries over the hulls.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Racing.OverlapGeometry.PlanformsMeet(Sim.Core.Racing.RrsSnapshot@,Sim.Core.Racing.RrsSnapshot@)
member.summary: Whether the two boats' plan-view footprints touch — the test that separates a boat come alongside from one running the other down, since only the latter has her bow over the other's deck as she crosses the line abeam.
member.remarks:
The rulebook has no such clause because it does not need one: a real bow cannot occupy the water a real transom is in, so "clear astern" and "alongside" cannot both be true of two real boats. A sim's hulls are 3D and overhang, and the shipped hull's stem head sits 8 cm above the transom's aftmost point and reaches 0.10 m past it in plan — a whole tenth of a metre of approach in which the line-abeam test alone says overlapped and the two are still apart in space. What this clause restores is the rulebook's unstated assumption, not a new rule. The design is docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-30-overlap-planform-definition-design.md.
Only should ask, and only about establishing an overlap. Two hulls in contact always share a point in plan, so at any touch this is true whatever the boats were doing on the way in — which is why it decides a transition and never a standing relation.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Racing.OverlapGeometry.RelationWhenNeitherIsClear(System.Single,System.Single)
member.summary: What to read for a pair the two-state definition has no answer for — one whose overlap was suppressed, so that neither boat is clear astern by the letter. Whichever lies further behind the other's line abeam reads astern; when neither does, which a suppression cannot produce but a dead heat can, and which is the only answer that reads the same from both boats.
member.remarks: Named for what it hands back rather than for the comparison it runs, because the comparison has a third outcome. For a rear-ender it gives the truth about where she is: her bow is a hand's breadth past the transom line (say −0.05 m) while the boat ahead is a full length past hers (−4.2 m), so she reads astern and rule 12 stays hers to answer. Deliberately a pure function of the two clearances — carrying the previous sample's answer forward instead agrees in every case that matters and costs this type the statelessness that lets a test hand it two positions.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Racing.OverlapGeometry.Separation_m(Sim.Core.Racing.RrsSnapshot@,Sim.Core.Racing.RrsSnapshot@)
member.summary: How far the pair is separated fore-and-aft, in metres: positive is the gap by which one is clear of the other, negative is how deep the overlap is. What the tracker's break margin is measured in — a relation alone cannot say whether a boat has just slipped past the line or is a length behind it. NaN for a pair this cannot measure, which is neither clear nor overlapped.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Racing.OverlapGeometry.Clearances(Sim.Core.Racing.RrsSnapshot@,Sim.Core.Racing.RrsSnapshot@)
member.summary: Both halves of the line-abeam test: how far lies behind 's line abeam, and the mirror. Positive is clear; the relation follows from the pair, and the deeper negative is how far into each other they are.
member.remarks: Public because a record of a ruling has to carry the numbers it turned on. Each boat's own bow and stern do NOT answer this — the query runs along the OTHER boat's fore axis, and the two part company for any pair that is not parallel — so a reader handed only the hull ends would re-derive a different verdict from the one that was given.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Racing.OverlapGeometry.Clearance(Sim.Core.Racing.RrsSnapshot@,Sim.Core.Racing.RrsSnapshot@)
member.summary: Metres by which 's hull lies behind the line abeam from 's aftmost point — positive when she is clear astern of it. Measured along the boat whose transom draws the line, because the rule names her line abeam, so it is her fore axis that orients it and not the pair's.
member.remarks: Both ends come off the hulls themselves, as support queries along that one axis. RRS asks where her hull reaches, not where her bow tip is, and the two part company the moment the pair is not parallel: at 45° a Laser's windward shoulder crosses the line abeam half a metre before her stem does. Taking the bow tip therefore under-read the overlap in exactly one direction — always toward clear astern, so always toward rule 12.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Racing.OverlapGeometry.Reach(Sim.Core.Geometry.PosedShape@,System.Numerics.Vector3,System.Numerics.Vector3)
member.summary: How far reaches along , taking the point that is farthest in . The two directions differ only when the aftmost point is wanted: it is found against the axis and still measured along it.

member.name: T:Sim.Core.Racing.OverlapRelation
member.summary: The resolved overlap of boat A relative to boat B, supplied to by a stateful resolver (the umpire, later). Overlap cannot be a pure instantaneous predicate — RRS hysteresis and the transitive "a boat between them overlaps both" clause both need state a pair alone lacks — so the kernel takes it as given. Rule 10 is opposite-tack and ignores it; rules 11/12 (P3) consume it. See spec §3.3.

member.name: F:Sim.Core.Racing.OverlapRelation.Unknown

member.name: F:Sim.Core.Racing.OverlapRelation.AClearAstern

member.name: T:Sim.Core.Racing.OverlapTracker
member.summary:
Resolves overlap across the whole fleet, once per umpire sample (spec §3.3). It exists because overlap is not a property of a pair in an instant, in two separate ways.
It has memory. RRS deems an established overlap to stand until it is broken, so a boat that surges a hand's breadth past the line abeam has not broken it. Breaking takes a real gap held for a real time — and .
It is transitive. Two boats are also overlapped when a boat between them overlaps both — a relation no pairwise kernel can see, because the boat that creates it is not in the pair. So this runs over the fleet and closes the relation, rather than answering pair by pair. The betweenness half of that clause is load-bearing, and says why.

member.name: F:Sim.Core.Racing.OverlapTracker._resolved
member.summary: Resolved relation per ordered pair, rebuilt each sample. Ordered so a reader can ask either way round without having to know which boat the tracker filed the pair under.

member.name: F:Sim.Core.Racing.OverlapTracker._resolvedLastSample
member.summary: The sample before this one's answers, kept whole so a touch that happened between the two can be judged by the relation that stood when it happened (#312). Swapped rather than copied, so carrying it costs a sample nothing.

member.name: F:Sim.Core.Racing.OverlapTracker._sampleTime_s

member.summary: When each of those two was published — together, how far back this tracker can answer. NaN before the first .

member.name: T:Sim.Core.Racing.OverlapTracker.PairState
member.summary: What this tracker carries for one pair of boats.
member.remarks:
One type rather than three collections keyed alike, so the lifecycle cannot be applied to two of them and forgotten for the third — the whole of and of is now one line each.
Having an entry at all is a fact in its own right: it means this tracker has looked at the pair before, which is what separates "she came up from astern and put her bow over the transom" from "they were overlapped the first time anyone looked" (see ).

member.name: F:Sim.Core.Racing.OverlapTracker.PairState.Relation
member.summary: This sample's direct relation, read from the lower-id boat. Refreshed every , unlike the two above it, and kept here so reads the answer the establishment pass reached rather than re-deriving one.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Racing.OverlapTracker.TryBetween(Sim.Core.BoatId,Sim.Core.BoatId,System.Single,Sim.Core.Racing.OverlapRelation@)
member.summary: The overlap of relative to as this tracker had it resolved at — this sample's answer, or the previous one for an earlier instant. False for an instant older than that, which this cannot answer for. , by contrast, is a real answer: the pair was not in that sample.
member.remarks:
The instant is a required argument because it is load-bearing and invisible when it is wrong — a foul is attributed by the relation as it stood at the touch, and a touch reaches the umpire up to a sample late (#312). Both readings are well-formed, so nothing downstream can notice the difference; only the boats would.
Out of reach fails rather than clamping, and it is not enough to answer : rule 10 does not consult the relation at all, so an opposite-tack pair would still be attributed off a stale instant. The counterpart half of the same verdict — — reaches 64 samples back, so only this side can tell the caller that the two halves no longer describe the same moment.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Racing.OverlapTracker.Reset
member.summary: Forget every resolution and all of the memory behind it — a race restart is not a moment the boats sailed through, so no overlap the last race established is still deemed to stand. Left behind, that memory ruled the new race's first second (#313, spec §3.5).

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Racing.OverlapTracker.EstablishedPairsThisSample(System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList{System.ValueTuple{Sim.Core.BoatId,Sim.Core.Racing.RrsSnapshot}},System.Single)
member.summary: The directly-overlapping pairs, after memory: geometry establishes an overlap the instant it appears, but only the margin held for the dwell takes one away.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Racing.OverlapTracker.Resolve(System.ValueTuple{Sim.Core.BoatId,Sim.Core.BoatId},Sim.Core.Racing.RrsSnapshot@,Sim.Core.Racing.RrsSnapshot@,System.Single)
member.summary: Carry this pair's state forward one sample and answer whether they end it overlapped: an overlap is established on sight of a crossing that counts, and only a proper break takes one away.
member.remarks:
Both boats' clearances are taken once here and everything is read off them — the relation, the break margin, and which boat is further behind are all functions of those two numbers, and taking them costs four support queries over hulls of several hundred vertices.
A pair the geometry cannot measure — a boat the host has not projected yet — leaves everything as it was, and does not count as having been seen. Folding that into "not overlapped" would let a boat with no hull silently break a real overlap, which is the same class of mistake as reading her as clear astern of the fleet.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Racing.OverlapTracker.Establishes(Sim.Core.Racing.OverlapTracker.PairState,System.Boolean,Sim.Core.Racing.RrsSnapshot@,Sim.Core.Racing.RrsSnapshot@)
member.summary: Whether this pair's line-abeam overlap is one the rule recognises. It is, unless what crossed the line was her bow over the other boat's deck rather than a hull come alongside — which is what meeting planforms mean, and which is the whole of .

remarks.para: A pair never seen before is exempt, and that is the rule. Boats already overlapped the first time this tracker looks at them — rails together at the gun, where nothing is judged until the fleet is racing — have no approach on record, so there is nothing to say the overlap arose from one boat running the other down. Suppressing it would leave them reading clear astern until they separated by the break margin, and would name one of them astern of the other on a hair's breadth of stagger.

The first clause is a short-circuit, not a second rule. An overlap already established stays established either way, because the caller only ever sets the flag on this answer and never clears it; what the clause saves is the GJK run, for the common case of two boats sailing along overlapped. Deleting it costs speed and changes no verdict.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Racing.OverlapTracker.HasBrokenClear(Sim.Core.Racing.OverlapTracker.PairState,System.Single,System.Single)
member.summary: Whether this pair has been clear by more than the margin for longer than the dwell — the two-part test that separates a real separation from a surge.

member.summary: The direct relation the establishment pass reached for this pair a moment ago, read in the order asked. Carried forward rather than re-derived: re-running the geometry here would repeat four support queries per pair, and would have to work out from the deemed groups whether an overlap it saw had been suppressed — a conclusion that holds only while nothing else can remove a pair from those groups.

member.name: T:Sim.Core.Racing.PairRelation
member.summary: One ordered pair's overlap as the fleet resolver settled it at one sample, with both halves of the line-abeam test it was settled from.

remarks.para: The numbers as well as the verdict, because the relation alone cannot say whether a boat has just slipped past the line abeam or is a length behind it — the difference between an overlap about to be established and two boats with nothing to do with each other.

and the clearances answer different questions and may disagree. The relation is what the rule DEEMS: it carries the established-overlap memory and the transitive clause. The clearances are this instant's geometry. A pair reading clear while the relation says overlapped is the memory or the closure at work, not an inconsistency — and it is exactly the row worth looking at.
Neither clearance is recoverable from the boats' own hull ends: the query runs along the OTHER boat's fore axis ().

member.name: T:Sim.Core.Racing.PartyWindow
member.summary: One boat's short rolling history of umpire samples — a fixed-capacity ring the umpire owns and shares across every encounter that boat is in (so a boat in several encounters is stored once, and its history is immutable data the encounters only read). The necessity walk-back reads and, via , the pre-maneuver sample. A lookback older than the buffer fails rather than clamping, so the walk-back stays blind instead of projecting across a gap it cannot see.

member.remarks: It reports no sample time, and no longer needs to. It briefly did, so a verdict could carry how far back it had reached — but a contact is judged from the touch itself now (#335), and the only remaining caller is the necessity walk-back, which asks for a specific past instant and has no use for how near it landed.

member.name: T:Sim.Core.Racing.Penalty
member.summary:
One penalty a boat has accrued: what it was for, and what it still owes. This is what a penalty readout draws a row from (#156) — the umpire's log cannot serve that alone, because a mark touch never passes through the umpire and so appears nowhere in it.
Both kinds fit one shape because the rulebook already names them: a mark touch is rule 31 (no counterpart boat, no beyond the touch itself), a Part 2 foul is rule 10 and carries the boat it was called against.

member.name: T:Sim.Core.Racing.PenaltyTracker
member.summary:
Tracks penalties and tack/gybe exoneration. A mark touch (rising edge, per-buoy 5 s bounce cooldown) accrues a One-Turn penalty under rule 31; an RRS Part 2 foul (posted by the umpire, #155) accrues a Two-Turns penalty via . A completed turn — a tack and a gybe within 30 s of each other — retires one turn from the oldest outstanding penalty; the penalty clears once its turns are all done. Each outstanding penalty is worth +60 s at the finish regardless of how many turns it owes. See docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-24-mark-penalties-design.md §7 and the RRS umpire design §3.6.
Which marks rule 31 covers is not asked here — see . This tracker knows nothing of legs, phases or course geometry; it debounces the touches it is handed and counts turns.
Cleared penalties are kept, not dropped: is the boat's record of everything it accrued, which is what a readout draws its rows from, and the mark touch appears nowhere else.

member.name: F:Sim.Core.Racing.PenaltyTracker.MarkTouchRule
member.summary: Touching a mark is RRS rule 31 — the rulebook's own name for it, which is what lets a mark touch and a Part 2 foul share one shape.

member.name: P:Sim.Core.Racing.PenaltyTracker.Penalties
member.summary: Everything this boat has accrued, oldest first, each with what it was for and what it still owes. Includes cleared penalties.

member.name: P:Sim.Core.Racing.PenaltyTracker.TurnsOwed
member.summary: Turns still to sail across every outstanding penalty — the figure that moves while a boat spins one off, which and both hide (a two-turns foul reads identically before and after its first turn).

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Racing.PenaltyTracker.Post(Sim.Core.Racing.PenaltyIncident@)
member.summary: Accrue the Part 2 foul the umpire confirmed against this boat. Takes the whole incident so the rule, cause and counterpart travel with the penalty rather than being reduced to a turn count the readout would then have to guess at.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Racing.PenaltyTracker.Update(System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyCollection{System.String},Sim.Core.Racing.ManeuverEvent,System.Single,System.Boolean)
member.param: The marks this boat is touching that rule 31 actually covers right now — its caller's answer, not every mark under the hull. Which marks those are is a question about the leg being sailed and the phase of the race (RRS 31 names a starting mark before starting, the marks of the leg being sailed, and a finishing mark after finishing), and answering it here would mean teaching this tracker the course geometry it is deliberately free of.

Whether this boat is racing, and so may sail penalty turns off. Kept a separate question from which touches count, because the two windows are not the same shape: a boat that has finished but not yet cleared the line is still racing under RRS — she can still take a penalty — while rule 31 has by then narrowed to the finishing marks alone.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Racing.PenaltyTracker.PartlySailedIndex
member.summary: The penalty currently being sailed off — outstanding, with at least one of its turns already done. There is at most one: turns retire oldest-first, so a second penalty is untouched until the one ahead of it clears.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Racing.PenaltyTracker.RestartLapsedSequence
member.summary: Put the half-sailed penalty back to owing every turn. The turns already made do not part-pay it — under RRS 44.2 an interrupted penalty was not taken, so it starts again.

member.name: T:Sim.Core.Racing.Proximity
member.summary: Pure closest-point-of-approach geometry over a snapshot pair (spec §3.2): the point-kinematic CPA distance and TCPA from the pair's current velocities. Feeds the umpire's relevance gate and necessity test; it never decides a rule, which is why it stays separate from — proximity is a tunable safety geometry, a verdict is a discrete rule outcome.

member.name: T:Sim.Core.Racing.ProximityGate
member.summary: Section A's relevance gate: a pair matters while it is within a query radius (tens of metres, spec §3.7). CPA does not enter here — under always-create an encounter exists for any candidate pair, so proximity is only asked "are they still close enough to care?"; the closing-CPA geometry lives solely in the necessity walk-back.

member.name: T:Sim.Core.Racing.RaceLine
member.summary: An oriented line the boat crosses, with a hysteresis band that debounces wave/leeway chatter. Built either as a finite (start/finish/gate-entry, bounded between two marks) or a one-sided (mark entry/exit, live on one side of its origin). Stateful: call each tick with the boat reference point; it returns +1 (crossed in the + direction), −1 (crossed against the normal), or 0. A crossing registers the instant the leading edge breaks the plane, and only where the foot lies within the line's span (segment endpoints / ray extent); the ± band re-arms rather than gates, which is what rejects chatter. A ray forgets the hull entirely while it is off the extent — see . See docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-23-race-course-time-trial-design.md §6.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Racing.RaceLine.PlaneNormal(System.Numerics.Vector2,System.Numerics.Vector2)
member.summary:
The unit crossing normal for a line declared from to — the direction a crossing counts as forward in, matching . Declaration order sets the sign, so anything needing to know which side of a start/finish plane a boat is on asks here rather than rotating the ends itself, and Dot(p - a, PlaneNormal(a, b)) is that side as a signed distance.
for a line whose ends coincide: it has no plane, and a zero normal reports every boat as ON it, which is the answer a caller can act on. Returning a NaN direction instead would make every comparison against the result false at once.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Racing.RaceLine.Segment(System.Numerics.Vector2,System.Numerics.Vector2,System.Numerics.Vector2,System.Single)
member.summary: Finite line between marks and , crossing positive in the + direction.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Racing.RaceLine.Ray(System.Numerics.Vector2,System.Numerics.Vector2,System.Numerics.Vector2,System.Single)
member.summary: One-sided ray from , live only on the side, crossing positive in +.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Racing.RaceLine.Update(System.Numerics.Vector2)
member.summary: Single-point crossing, for a caller with no hull — tests, and anything tracking a reference point rather than a body.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Racing.RaceLine.Update(Sim.Core.Geometry.PosedShape@)
member.summary: Hull-aware crossing: the leading edge is the hull's furthest point along the normal, so "any part breaks the plane". Returns +1 / −1 / 0; see class summary.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Racing.RaceLine.Advance(System.Single,System.Numerics.Vector2)
member.summary: The crossing state machine, shared by both entry points: they differ only in how far the hull reaches, never in what a crossing means.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Racing.RaceLine.IsWhollyBeyond(Sim.Core.Geometry.PosedShape@)
member.summary:
Whether the whole hull lies past the plane in the + direction — the trailing-edge counterpart of 's "any part breaks the plane". Stateless: this is a question about a pose, not an event, so it neither arms nor fires the line.
The plane only, not the span between the marks: a boat that has crossed and sailed on past the pin end is beyond the line. RRS pairs clearing the line with clearing its marks, and the marks are the caller's question — this line does not know where they are now, only where they were laid.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Racing.RaceLine.LeadingEdge(Sim.Core.Geometry.PosedShape@)
member.summary: The hull's leading edge on the normal, and the point it sits at. Broad-phase: a bounding sphere clear of the line answers with its centre in one dot product; otherwise the hull's own support point, so "any part breaks the plane".

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Racing.RaceLine.FlatSupport(Sim.Core.Geometry.PosedShape@,System.Numerics.Vector2)
member.summary: How far the hull reaches along a plan direction. The line is a vertical plane, so the direction carries no z and the support point's height cannot affect the answer — which is why this measure is identical to the old flattened one for any normal a race line actually uses, and differs only where a heeled hull's true extreme is a bilge rather than a deck edge.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Racing.RaceLine.ReachOf(Sim.Core.Geometry.PosedShape@)
member.summary:
Where this hull stands against the line right now. Stateless, like : a question about a pose, so it neither arms nor fires the line.
One reading answers the three the starting rules ask, which is why they share a method rather than each getting a predicate that could drift from the others: Beyond_m > 0 && WithinSpan is rule 29.1's "on the course side of the starting line"; Beyond_m > 0 alone is rule 30.1's wider "the line or one of its extensions"; and Beyond_m <= 0 is "her hull is completely on the pre-start side", which takes flag X down.
It measures the hull's furthest point along the normal — the same point fires on, and so the LAST part of her to leave the course side. That is what makes "any part of her is over" and "all of her is back" one number's sign instead of two support queries that disagree at the boundary.
Deliberately without 's bounding-sphere shortcut, and the reason is rather than the distance. In the far field that shortcut answers with the hull's centre, so the foot it reports can fall outside the span while the true support point is inside it — and rule 29.1 turns on exactly that difference. (The sign of would survive the shortcut, which is why a crossing can use it; do not reinstate it here on the strength of that.)

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Racing.RaceLine.Reset

member.param: The point itself. Carried because it is the answer to the expensive half of the question — a support query is a linear scan of the hull's whole collision cloud — and any line sharing this one's normal can be advanced with it instead of asking again.

member.name: T:Sim.Core.Racing.RaceOutcome
member.summary: How a boat's race ended. Appendix A10's own vocabulary, trimmed to what this sim can actually produce — a code is added when something can reach it, not because the rulebook lists it.
member.remarks:
Deliberately not part of . A phase says where she is on the course and is 's to decide; an outcome says how her race ended and is the race's. Folding one into the other would push the starting rules into a tracker that is otherwise fed nothing but a hull and a clock.
ZFP is not here on purpose. A boat carrying rule 30.2's 20% still finishes, so it is a penalty on a finisher rather than an outcome; it travels beside this as a count, because a restart can add another.

member.name: F:Sim.Core.Racing.RaceOutcome.Racing
member.summary: Still sailing, and still able to change her result. The default, so a fleet that has not started yet reads as racing rather than as anything having happened to it.

member.name: F:Sim.Core.Racing.RaceOutcome.Finished
member.summary: She finished — and cleared, which is where RRS ends her race rather than at the crossing.

member.name: F:Sim.Core.Racing.RaceOutcome.Ocs
member.summary: A10: "did not start; on the course side of the starting line at her starting signal and failed to start, or broke rule 30.1." One code for both, as the rulebook intends: the I-flag boat who never rounds an end and the P-flag boat who never returns have done the same thing, which is fail to start.

member.name: F:Sim.Core.Racing.RaceOutcome.Dns
member.summary: A10: "did not start (other than DNC and OCS)" — she was never over anything, she simply never crossed.

member.name: F:Sim.Core.Racing.RaceOutcome.Ufd
member.summary: Rule 30.3: disqualified without a hearing under the U flag. Rule 36 does not carry it into a restart.

member.name: F:Sim.Core.Racing.RaceOutcome.Bfd
member.summary: Rule 30.4: disqualified without a hearing under the black flag. Rule 36 carries this one into a restart, and bars her from sailing it.

member.name: F:Sim.Core.Racing.RaceOutcome.Ret
member.summary: She retired. A result in its own right, not an absence of one — beating her still counts.

member.name: T:Sim.Core.Racing.RaceStanding
member.summary: One boat's line in the fleet standings: where it lies, how far behind the leader, and — once it is home — what it took. Assembled live, so the same row serves the running order and the final result.
member.remarks: A finished boat carries zero. That is the caller's to honour and cannot be inferred from the race tracker's active index, which still points at the Finish feature after the crossing rather than running off the end of the course.

member.name: P:Sim.Core.Racing.RaceStanding.Outcome

member.name: P:Sim.Core.Racing.RaceStanding.Finished

member.name: P:Sim.Core.Racing.RaceStanding.Interval_s
member.summary: Corrected time behind the boat that finished immediately before this one; zero for the first finisher and for anyone still racing. Filled by .

member.name: P:Sim.Core.Racing.RaceStanding.Corrected_s
member.summary: Elapsed time with every penalty served — the time that decides a finisher's place. Both kinds fall due here: the flat charge per outstanding turns penalty, and rule 30.2's 20%.

member.name: P:Sim.Core.Racing.RaceStanding.RankingGroup
member.summary: Which band of the fleet she is ranked in, before anything inside it is compared. Finishers, then boats still sailing, then boats whose race is over — because a boat who is out cannot finish, so she cannot outrank one that still might, however far back that boat is.
member.remarks: Deliberately not a comparison on alone. A boat who is out has no distance left to sail, so the old "everyone unfinished is ranked on distance remaining" rule read her zero as a boat about to cross the line and put her at the head of the fleet.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Racing.RaceStanding.Rank(System.Collections.Generic.List{Sim.Core.Racing.RaceStanding})
member.summary: Sort into running order, then stamp each boat's and its interval to the boat immediately ahead.
member.remarks: Two regimes, and the seam is deliberate. Boats still on the water are ranked on distance left alone: a penalty is a debt that falls due at the finish, and letting it reorder the fleet mid-race would put the readout at odds with what the player sees out of the boat. Boats that have crossed are ranked on corrected time, which is the real result, and always sit ahead of boats still racing. Anything that cannot be separated falls back to boat id, so a tied pair does not reshuffle itself on every refresh.

member.name: T:Sim.Core.Racing.RaceState
member.summary: Immutable per-tick snapshot for the HUD. See spec §8. is one signed clock: negative through the pre-start countdown (e.g. −120 → 0), zero at the gun, positive during the race (= elapsed race time). NaN before a start is armed (legacy first-crossing mode counts it from the crossing). It runs on past the finishing crossing, because RRS does — she is racing until she clears, and is what her race took.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Racing.RaceState.#ctor(Sim.Core.Racing.RacePhase,System.Single,System.Single,System.Int32,System.Int32,System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList{System.Boolean})
member.summary: Immutable per-tick snapshot for the HUD. See spec §8. is one signed clock: negative through the pre-start countdown (e.g. −120 → 0), zero at the gun, positive during the race (= elapsed race time). NaN before a start is armed (legacy first-crossing mode counts it from the crossing). It runs on past the finishing crossing, because RRS does — she is racing until she clears, and is what her race took.

member.name: T:Sim.Core.Racing.RaceTracker
member.summary: Drives the boat through the course feature-by-feature and runs one signed race clock. Exactly one feature is active at a time; it completes when its signed counter reaches its target. With a start armed () the Start line only completes at/after the start time and the clock reads from it (a real pre-start countdown: negative before, positive after); a boat over early must return to the pre-start side and cross again. Without an armed start the first crossing starts the clock (legacy). The Finish crossing freezes the clock (→Finished). Pure and deterministic — fed only (boatXY, t). See spec §8.

member.name: P:Sim.Core.Racing.RaceTracker.RaceTimer
member.summary: Signed race clock: negative counting down to the gun, positive elapsed race time after. NaN until a start is armed and (legacy) the first crossing. It does not stop at the finish — RRS keeps a boat racing until she clears, and she may yet have to sail turns and re-cross, so what her race took is and not this.

member.name: P:Sim.Core.Racing.RaceTracker.FinishTime_s
member.summary: Elapsed time at the finishing crossing, or NaN before one. Provisional while she is still on the line: a penalty in that window voids it, and the crossing that follows her turns stamps a new one. It stops moving for good when she clears — which is the caller's to observe, since clearing is a question about the hull and the marks that this tracker cannot see.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Racing.RaceTracker.ArmStart(System.Single)
member.summary: Arm the pre-start clock: the timer hits 0 at (the Start line goes live then; a boat already across it at the gun is over early and must return to the pre-start side to cross again). Pass e.g. t + 120 for a 2-minute countdown, which reads −120 now.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Racing.RaceTracker.Update(System.Numerics.Vector2,System.Single,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Single-point convenience, for a caller with no hull.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Racing.RaceTracker.Update(Sim.Core.Geometry.PosedShape@,System.Single,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Score this tick against the hull itself.
member.param: The definition of Start's middle clause — "and having complied with rule 30.1 if it applies". A parameter rather than a rule this tracker knows, so it stays a course-progress machine fed nothing but a hull and a clock: which flag is flying, and what it costs, is 's business. Pass true where rule 30.1 does not apply, which is every start but an I-flag one.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Racing.RaceTracker.Advance(System.Int32,System.Single,System.Boolean)
member.summary: What both entry points do once the feature has been scored. Taking the delta by value rather than a scoring delegate keeps this allocation-free: it runs per boat per tick at 500 Hz, where a captured closure would be garbage on every one of them.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Racing.RaceTracker.SatisfiedThisTick(Sim.Core.Racing.CourseFeature,System.Int32,System.Single,System.Boolean)
member.summary:
Whether this tick satisfies the active feature. A line is crossed and a mark is rounded, and the two are satisfied by different things — merging them into one counter test is what stranded boats twice (#301, #306).
A line completes on the crossing: one pass through the span in the scoring direction. Nothing before it nets against it, because the counter counts crossings and is not a reading of which side she is on — she can change sides without touching the span at all by sailing round an end, which rule 29.1 expressly allows ("the pre-start side of the starting line or one of its extensions"). Ask it for a level instead and an ordinary pre-start strands her: out past the committee end, back above the line, dip down through it to set up, and she is a crossing in debt with no way to start. A boat over early is likewise not started by sitting there — she starts when she next crosses, which is what RRS asks of her.
A rounding completes on its counter, which is the one thing the counter is for: an ordered pair of ray crossings, where going round the other way genuinely does have to be unwound. zeroes it per feature, so no rounding inherits another's debt.
The gun belongs to the Start alone: RRS has a boat start when any part of her hull crosses to the course side at or after the starting signal. With no sequence armed the start time is NaN and the first crossing starts her (legacy).
And so does rule 30.1. Under an I flag a boat over in the last minute must round an end before any crossing counts, so a crossing alone is not a start — which is the one way the crossing-completes-the-line rule above is too permissive, and the reason exists.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Racing.RaceTracker.CrossTheFinish(System.Single)
member.summary: Take the finish, provisionally. The feature is deliberately not advanced past: a finish is undone by a penalty until the boat clears, and needs this line still to be the active one. The clock keeps running — only is stamped here.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Racing.RaceTracker.VoidFinish
member.summary: Undo the finish: she is racing again, owes her turns, and must re-cross. RRS un-finishes a boat that answers for a breach after crossing, so the crossing she already made does not count.
member.remarks:
The counter is left exactly as it is, which looks wrong and is deliberate. It still reads "satisfied", because she is still on the far side of the line — and that is harmless, because fires on the crossing rather than on the level, so no amount of sitting there re-takes the finish. What re-takes it is another crossing from the course side, which is precisely what RRS asks of her; how she gets back to that side is not the rule's business.
And must not be called, tempting as it looks. Arming clears each line's last-known side, so her run back to the course side would leave the line unarmed and the crossing that follows would score nothing — she could not re-finish at all. Her crossing state is not stale; it is the record of where she actually is.

member.name: T:Sim.Core.Racing.RightOfWay
member.summary: The pure rulebook relation: given a pair (and a supplied overlap relation), which boat must keep clear and under which rule. Instantaneous, no history, no fouls — the stateful umpire polls it each sample and owns the timeline, rule 14 and exoneration. P1 implements only rule 10 (opposite tacks). See spec §3.2.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Racing.RightOfWay.Verdict(Sim.Core.Racing.RrsSnapshot@,Sim.Core.Racing.RrsSnapshot@,Sim.Core.Racing.OverlapRelation)
member.param: Resolved overlap of A relative to B. Rule 10 is opposite-tack and does not consult it; it is carried so the call shape is stable when rules 11/12 arrive (P3).

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Racing.RightOfWay.SameTack(Sim.Core.Racing.RrsSnapshot@,Sim.Core.Racing.RrsSnapshot@,Sim.Core.Racing.OverlapRelation)
member.summary: Rules 11 and 12 — the same-tack pair, split by whether they are overlapped. Both need the resolved relation, so an unresolved one is no verdict rather than a guess.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Racing.RightOfWay.WindwardOf(Sim.Core.Racing.RrsSnapshot@,Sim.Core.Racing.RrsSnapshot@)
member.summary: Which of an overlapped same-tack pair is the windward boat — the one lying on the other's windward side — or null when neither is.
member.remarks:
Windward is a question about sides, not about distance up the wind axis: RRS says a boat's leeward side is the side away from the wind she is sailing on, and of two overlapped same-tack boats the one on the other's leeward side is the leeward boat. The two readings agree for a near-parallel pair, which is most of what rule 11 judges, and come apart as their headings diverge — same tack, one beating and one reaching — because her centreline rotates out from under the wind axis while the wind axis does not move.
No wind vector is needed to answer it. Rule 11 only ever judges a same-tack pair, so the tack itself names the side the wind is on. That is faithful rather than merely convenient: names the tack by boom side, which is exactly how RRS resolves the awkward case — "when sailing by the lee or directly downwind, her leeward side is the side on which her mainsail lies" — so a boat sailing by the lee comes out right here, where a projection along the wind would have her backwards.
Against the sum of the pair's two windward beams rather than either boat's own centreline, so the verdict cannot depend on which boat the umpire happened to pass first. Null, not a default party, when neither is to the other's side: the tie is the one place the sign flip that swapping the pair produces would otherwise name opposite hulls for the same instant, and it is also the honest answer, since a boat dead ahead on the centreline is on no side at all.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Racing.RightOfWay.WindwardBeam(Sim.Core.Racing.RrsSnapshot@)
member.summary: The direction of a boat's windward side as RRS defines it: the side opposite her mainsail, which is what her tack names — starboard tack means the boom is out to port, so her windward side is starboard.
member.remarks: Stated from the mainsail rather than from the breeze on purpose. Normally the two are the same thing, but sailing by the lee or dead downwind the wind crosses what is still her leeward side, and RRS resolves that by naming the mainsail's side outright. Describing this as "the beam the wind comes over" would therefore be wrong in exactly the case the boom-side definition exists to get right.

member.name: F:Sim.Core.Racing.RightOfWay.LevelTolerance
member.summary: Below this the pair reads as level, neither to the other's side. In metres against the summed unit beams, so ~2× their real athwartships offset — a millimetre of it, which is noise rather than a windward boat.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Racing.RightOfWay.Rule13(Sim.Core.Racing.RrsSnapshot@,Sim.Core.Racing.RrsSnapshot@)
member.summary: Rule 13: after passing head to wind, she keeps clear until she is on a close-hauled course. When both are subject to it at once, the second sentence decides between them.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Racing.RightOfWay.BothTackingGiveWay(Sim.Core.Racing.RrsSnapshot@,Sim.Core.Racing.RrsSnapshot@)
member.summary: Rule 13's second sentence — "the one on the other's port side or the one astern shall keep clear". Read as one test with a fallback rather than two competing ones: side is the question whenever there is a side to be on, and bow to stern there is not, so the pair in line falls through to astern.

member.name: F:Sim.Core.Racing.RightOfWay.InLineTolerance_m
member.summary: Lateral separation below which the pair reads as bow-to-stern rather than side by side, so rule 13's "or the one astern" takes over. A hull's beam, near enough — narrower and a boat directly astern starts being called a side-by-side pair on solver noise alone.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Racing.RightOfWay.PortBeam(System.Numerics.Vector2)
member.summary: The port-beam direction for a boat on — her fore axis turned 90° to port (left), which in this world frame is +Z × forward.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Racing.RightOfWay.StarboardBeam(System.Numerics.Vector2)
member.summary: Her starboard beam — the other way round.

member.name: T:Sim.Core.Racing.RightOfWayVerdict
member.summary: A Section-A right-of-way verdict: which boat must keep clear, and under which rule number — the call an umpire actually makes ("broke rule 10"), so a later RuleApplication can attribute the foul. means no implemented rule makes a determination for this pair yet.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Racing.RightOfWayVerdict.#ctor(Sim.Core.Racing.Party,System.Int32)
member.summary: A Section-A right-of-way verdict: which boat must keep clear, and under which rule number — the call an umpire actually makes ("broke rule 10"), so a later RuleApplication can attribute the foul. means no implemented rule makes a determination for this pair yet.

member.name: T:Sim.Core.Racing.RrsRules
member.summary: Human names for the rules the umpire can call. A readout showing only "r12" names the rule and says nothing about what it was, and rule numbers are exactly what someone new to racing has not memorised.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Racing.RrsRules.ShortName(System.Int32)
member.summary: One word for what the penalised boat was when the duty fell on her — not what she did wrong. The row this labels already sits on her record and already says how it happened, so "r11 windward" reads as "you were the windward boat", and the duty is the rule's to state. Empty for a rule with no name yet, so a caller degrades to the bare number rather than showing a meaning nobody wrote.

member.name: T:Sim.Core.Racing.RrsSnapshot
member.summary: One boat's RRS-relevant facts at one umpire sample — the pure input to the right-of-way verdict and proximity. A value type built from what a participant already projects. It grows by phase as added init properties, never a changed call shape: P1 carries what rule 10 and proximity read (tack, position, velocity) plus the hull and fore-aft axis the same-tack overlap rules consume; the close-hauled flag (r13), proper course and heading rate (Section B) arrive later. See docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-17-rrs-umpire-design.md §3.1.

member.name: P:Sim.Core.Racing.RrsSnapshot.Tack
member.summary: Port / Starboard, or while between tacks (no defined tack — rule 10 makes no determination then).

member.name: P:Sim.Core.Racing.RrsSnapshot.Position
member.summary: Where this boat is in the world XY plane: her hull's own centre. The kinematic origin for proximity, and the point rules 11 and 13 compare athwartships to say which boat lies on the other's side — so it has to mean the same place on every hull.

member.name: P:Sim.Core.Racing.RrsSnapshot.Velocity
member.summary: World-XY velocity.

member.name: P:Sim.Core.Racing.RrsSnapshot.ForeAxis
member.summary: Unit fore-aft (bow) direction in world XY. Feeds the same-tack overlap geometry (r11/r12, P3); carried from P1 so the snapshot shape is stable.

member.name: P:Sim.Core.Racing.RrsSnapshot.Hull
member.summary: This boat's hull at this instant — what the line-abeam test measures. Null before the host has projected her, which answers for rather than treating as a boat of no length.
member.remarks: The hull itself rather than a length and a pair of offsets, for the reason RaceLine already asks it directly (commit c0eb0d0): RRS asks where her hull reaches, and a support query answers that exactly, at any attitude, from the same shape the renderer draws. Reducing her to a bow point on her centreline lost her beam, and a hull carries her shoulder across a line abeam before her bow tip gets there.

member.name: T:Sim.Core.Racing.RuleApplication

In P1 exactly one is ever live (rule 10); the two-level shape exists so later phases can stack several at once (at a mark, r18 on r11). is the acquisition stamp Section B's r15 grace window will read.

member.name: T:Sim.Core.Racing.Signals.SignalAudience
member.summary: Who a signal speaks to. Rule 29.1's X is the only one that does not address the whole fleet — the committee flies it when someone is over, but only the boats actually over are named.

member.name: T:Sim.Core.Racing.Signals.PreparatoryFlag
member.summary: The preparatory options of rule 26. is a combination, not a flag — the Race Signals plate shows five preparatory designs, and Z with I means Z and I flown together, so it hoists two signals and has no or asset of its own.

member.name: T:Sim.Core.Racing.Signals.RaceSignals
member.summary: What the race committee is flying. Producers report facts and signal decisions; this decides which flags fly and for how long.

member.name: F:Sim.Core.Racing.Signals.RaceSignals.RestartWarningDelay_s
member.summary: Rule 29.2: the warning signal for a restart is made one minute after First Substitute is removed. Unlike 29.1's cap this is measured from an event the committee times, which is why the module needs absolute time rather than the signed race clock.

member.name: F:Sim.Core.Racing.Signals.RaceSignals.IndividualRecallCap_s
member.summary: Rule 29.1 removes flag X no later than four minutes after the starting signal, whatever the boats do. Because the race clock is signed and zero at the gun, that cap needs no timestamp of its own — it is a bound on the clock the module is already ticked with.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Racing.Signals.RaceSignals.ArmStartSequence(Sim.Core.Racing.Signals.StartSequence,System.Single)

member.summary: The committee's outstanding course decisions — grouped so their lifetime is one thing to clear rather than two loose flags.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Racing.Signals.RaceSignals.CourseSignalState.#ctor(System.Boolean,System.Nullable{Sim.Core.Racing.Signals.CourseChange})

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Racing.Signals.RaceSignals.SignalAbandonment
member.summary: Rules 27.3 / 32.3: the committee abandons the race. The fleet stops racing at the signal; only a fresh puts them back in one.

member.name: P:Sim.Core.Racing.Signals.RaceSignals.StartVoided
member.summary:
Whether the committee has taken this start away from the fleet — a general recall or an abandonment. RRS ends the racing window at either, and only a fresh reopens it.
Deliberately not "is a recall flag flying": rule 29.2 has First Substitute come down a minute before the restart's warning signal, and the boats are plainly not racing in that minute. Reading the flag's visibility would put them back in a race that no longer exists.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Racing.Signals.RaceSignals.SignalShortenedCourse
member.summary: Rule 32.2: the course has been shortened.

member.name: P:Sim.Core.Racing.Signals.RaceSignals.WarningSignalDueAt_s

member.name: P:Sim.Core.Racing.Signals.RaceSignals.Changes

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Racing.Signals.RaceSignals.Reset
member.summary: Clear everything — armed sequence, previous hoist, pending movements. A re-arm after this re-reports whatever is flying as fresh hoists: a restart is a new sequence, not a continuation of the old one.

member.name: T:Sim.Core.Racing.Signals.SignalChange
member.summary: One flag movement on the committee hoist. Rule 26 attaches a sound to every movement, so this is what an audio layer subscribes to as well as what drives the hoist animation.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Racing.Signals.SignalChange.#ctor(Sim.Core.Racing.Signals.SignalFlag,Sim.Core.Racing.Signals.SignalMotion)

member.name: T:Sim.Core.Racing.Signals.SignalFlag
member.summary: Every flag the race committee can fly. One value per design: there is no Z-with-I entry, because that option hoists and together.

member.name: T:Sim.Core.Racing.Signals.StartSequence
member.summary: How one start is run: rule 26's milestone offsets and the preparatory flag flown. Offsets are signed seconds relative to the starting signal at 0, matching the race clock's own convention, so a milestone test is a direct comparison against it.
member.remarks:
Only is the rulebook's own sequence. Rule 26 marks its five-minute warning "or as stated in the notice of race or sailing instructions", which is what makes the shortened presets legitimate rather than invented: the sim is its own race committee and these are its sailing instructions. Rule 25.2 is the boundary — the signals' meanings may not be changed, only the times.
Every preset is symmetric about the preparatory flag: the gap from the warning signal to the preparatory equals the gap from the one-minute signal to the gun, as it does in rule 26's own 5-4-1-0. That symmetry is the shape a sailor internalises, so keeping it means learning one start teaches them all. It is pinned by a test rather than left to whoever edits these numbers next.

member.name: F:Sim.Core.Racing.Signals.StartSequence.StartingWindow_s
member.summary:
How long after the gun a boat may still start. Unstarted at this point she is scored — OCS if she was over or owed rule 30.1, DNS if she simply never crossed.
There is no such rule in the RRS, and it is worth saying so plainly rather than leaving someone to hunt for it: nothing in the book stops a boat returning and starting at any time. The only time limit there is rule 35's, which governs sailing the course and is itself optional ("the time limit for that race, if any"). This is a sailing instruction, on the same footing as the shortened sequences above.
It is rule 29.1's cap on flag X, and reads it from there rather than restating the number: when the committee stops flying X at a boat it has given up identifying her, which is the natural moment her chance to start runs out. Two literals documented to be the same number are two literals that can drift.

member.name: T:Sim.Core.Racing.Starting.StartingPenaltyTracker
member.summary:
Rule 30's starting penalties for one boat, together with rule 29.1's observation of her being over early. The two live here rather than apart because they are one reading of one hull against one line, taken once a tick — splitting them would mean two units asking the same question and drifting on the answer.
Pure and deterministic: fed only the hull and the clock, exactly as is. What the flag costs a boat is decided here; what the committee flies about it is ' own.

member.name: F:Sim.Core.Racing.Starting.StartingPenaltyTracker._sequence
member.summary: The armed start, or null before one. Held whole rather than picked apart into a flag and a window offset: they are two readings of one thing, set together and meaningless apart, and splitting them meant two fields that had to agree and reset asymmetrically.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Racing.Starting.StartingPenaltyTracker.ArmStart(System.Single,Sim.Core.Racing.Signals.StartSequence)
member.summary: Arm this start: the gun falls at , and says both which of rule 30's rules are in play and when its window opens.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Racing.Starting.StartingPenaltyTracker.Update(Sim.Core.Geometry.PosedShape@,System.Single)
member.summary: Read this boat's hull against the starting line for this tick.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Racing.Starting.StartingPenaltyTracker.SampleTheGun(Sim.Core.Racing.LineReach,System.Single)
member.summary: Rule 29.1's first limb, which is a question about one instant — "when at a boat's starting signal any part of her hull is on the course side" — and so is asked once, at the first tick the gun has fallen, and never revisited.
member.remarks: is what keeps this to the line proper. A boat past the plane but beyond an end is outside the line rather than on the course side of it, and 29.1 does not reach her: the rule that does is 30.1, which names the extensions expressly.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Racing.Starting.StartingPenaltyTracker.TriggerRoundTheEnds(Sim.Core.Racing.LineReach,System.Boolean)
member.summary: Rule 30.1's trigger: "any part of a boat's hull is on the course side of the starting line OR ONE OF ITS EXTENSIONS during the last minute before her starting signal". Wider than being over at the gun in both directions -- it reads the unbounded plane rather than the line proper, and it latches on any moment in the window rather than on the instant the gun fires. So a boat can owe this having been back well before the start, and having never been OCS at all.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Racing.Starting.StartingPenaltyTracker.InTheLastMinute(System.Single)
member.summary:
Rule 30's window, shared by 30.1, 30.2, 30.3 and 30.4: "during the last minute before her starting signal". Rule 26 marks that minute with the one-minute signal -- the preparatory flag coming down -- which is what this reads, rather than a literal sixty seconds.
The difference only shows on the shortened sequences, and there it is the whole ball game. They are sailing instructions that compress rule 26's shape, so a fixed 60 s opens the window before the preparatory flag is hoisted -- and in the 30-second preset, before the warning signal, so from the very first tick of the sequence. Rule 30 begins "If a black flag HAS BEEN DISPLAYED"; disqualifying her before it goes up is indefensible, and she is not yet racing either. For rule 26's own sequence the one-minute signal is at -60, so nothing about the rulebook case changes.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Racing.Starting.StartingPenaltyTracker.JudgeTheTriangle(Sim.Core.Geometry.PosedShape@,Sim.Core.Racing.LineReach,System.Boolean)
member.summary:
Rules 30.2, 30.3 and 30.4, which differ in what they cost and in nothing else: "no part of a boat's hull shall be in the triangle formed by the ends of the starting line and the first mark during the last minute before her starting signal".
She is identified once per attempt, not once per tick. 30.2's second 20% is for "a subsequent attempt to start the same race" -- a restart, which re-arms this -- so charging her again for still being there a tick later would invent a penalty the rule does not give.

member.name: P:Sim.Core.Racing.Starting.StartingPenaltyTracker.TrianglePenalty
member.summary: What being identified in the triangle costs under the flag flying, or null where the triangle is not a place she may not be. stands for rule 30.2's scoring penalty: it is the one consequence that does not end her race.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Racing.Starting.StartingPenaltyTracker.AnswerRoundTheEnds(Sim.Core.Racing.LineReach)
member.summary: Rule 30.1's discharge: "she shall sail across an extension so that her hull is completely on the pre-start side before she starts". One event answers both clauses, because an extension is normalled with the line: a crossing against that normal fires exactly when the hull's furthest point INTO the course side -- the last part of her still over -- goes pre-start, at a foot outside the span. Dipping back through the line itself is off every extension's extent and scores nothing, which is precisely what the rule refuses.
member.remarks:
Every extension is advanced, never short-circuited: they are stateful, and a ray that missed a tick would have the wrong side latched when the boat next came back to it.
Fed the support point the start line already found rather than the hull, because the extensions are built with the line's own normal — so asking each of them for the hull's furthest point along it would recompute, twice, the scan just did over the whole collision cloud. It is also the more precise of the two: the hull overload's bounding-sphere shortcut can hand the state machine a hull centre instead of the true support point.

member.name: P:Sim.Core.Racing.Starting.StartingPenaltyTracker.UnderTheRecallFlag
member.summary: Rule 29.1's two limbs, which several rules read together: on the course side of the line at the gun, or she must comply with rule 30.1.

member.name: P:Sim.Core.Racing.Starting.StartingPenaltyTracker.RoundTheEndsApplies
member.summary: Rule 30.1 is flown by I -- and by Z with I, which is a combination of the two rather than a flag of its own, so it carries both consequences.

member.name: P:Sim.Core.Racing.Starting.StartingPenaltyTracker.OwesRoundTheEnds
member.summary: Whether she still owes rule 30.1 -- the clause the definition of Start hangs on ("and having complied with rule 30.1 if it applies").

member.name: P:Sim.Core.Racing.Starting.StartingPenaltyTracker.IsOverEarly
member.summary: Whether rule 29.1 has something outstanding against this boat — what is told. She is answered for once her hull "has been completely on the pre-start side", which the rule states in the perfect tense and so is a latch: crossing to start afterwards does not put her back under the flag.
member.remarks: Rule 29.1 names two reasons and this carries both: on the course side of the line at the gun, or she must comply with rule 30.1. Which is why an I-flag start does not suppress X but creates cases for it.

Written as the rule reads rather than as the removal condition negated: still owing rule 30.1 is on its own enough to keep the flag up, and otherwise it is up while she was over at the gun and has not since been completely on the pre-start side.

member.name: P:Sim.Core.Racing.Starting.StartingPenaltyTracker.OutcomeIfSheNeverStarts
member.summary: What she is scored if the starting window closes with her still unstarted. Appendix A10 keeps the two apart and so does this: OCS is "on the course side of the starting line at her starting signal and failed to start, or broke rule 30.1", while a boat who was never over anything and simply never crossed is DNS.
member.remarks: Read off whether she is still owing rule 30.1, not whether she ever did: a boat who rounded an end as the rule asks has not broken it, so if she then never crosses she simply did not start.

member.name: P:Sim.Core.Racing.Starting.StartingPenaltyTracker.ScoringPenalties
member.summary: Rule 30.2's 20% penalties. A count rather than a flag: "if she is similarly identified during a subsequent attempt to start the same race, she shall receive an ADDITIONAL 20%".

member.name: P:Sim.Core.Racing.Starting.StartingPenaltyTracker.Disqualification
member.summary: Her disqualification under rule 30.3 (UFD) or 30.4 (BFD), or null if she has none. Not exonerable by anything she does on the water -- what clears it is a restart, and only for UFD.

member.name: F:Sim.Core.Racing.Starting.StartingPenaltyTracker.ScoringPenaltyFraction
member.summary: Rule 30.2's fraction, as the sim charges it: 20%. See for why it is a count rather than an amount.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Racing.Starting.StartingPenaltyTracker.Reset
member.summary:
Forget this attempt and re-arm for the next one.
What survives is what rule 36 lets a restart of the same race carry: a breach of the original "shall not cause a boat to be penalized except under rule 2, 30.2, 30.4", so the scoring penalties stand and a black flag stands, while a U-flag disqualification is forgiven. Starting a fresh race carries nothing at all, and its caller says so by following this with — which keeps rule 36, a race-level rule, out of a tracker that otherwise knows only a hull and a clock.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Racing.Starting.StartingPenaltyTracker.ForgiveStartingPenalties
member.summary: Rules 30.2 and 30.4: "but NOT if it is postponed or abandoned before the starting signal". The one thing that wipes a starting penalty clean.

member.name: T:Sim.Core.Racing.Starting.StartingTriangle
member.summary: Rule 30's triangle — "the triangle formed by the ends of the starting line and the first mark" — against which rules 30.2, 30.3 and 30.4 all ask the same question: is any part of her hull in it. One predicate, three consequences.
member.remarks:
Held as a vertical prism rather than a flat plan figure, and tested with . The rule is about a hull, and a hull floats, heels and pitches, so a flat triangle at z = 0 would answer "no" for a boat sitting squarely in it — two convex bodies in 3D overlap only if they meet in every axis. Extruding it past any height a hull can reach makes the height irrelevant, which is what the rule intends.
Exact, via the narrow phase the sim already ships, rather than a hand-rolled separating-axis test. A support-only SAT over the triangle's three edges is necessary but not sufficient for convex bodies, and where it goes wrong is the near-touching configurations — which here decide a disqualification.

member.name: F:Sim.Core.Racing.Starting.StartingTriangle.HalfHeight_m
member.summary: Half the prism's height. Far above anything a hull reaches, so the plan figure is all that decides the answer, and far below, so a submerged appendage cannot slip under it.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Racing.Starting.StartingTriangle.Contains(Sim.Core.Geometry.PosedShape@)
member.summary: Whether any part of this hull is in the triangle.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Racing.Starting.StartingTriangle.MightReach(Sim.Core.Geometry.PosedShape@)
member.summary: Broad phase, so the narrow phase only runs for a boat anywhere near the start. A whole fleet is asked this every tick of the last minute.

member.summary: The last tack she actually established, or null if she never has — a boat that has not sailed, or one just re-seated. Null rather than a default side: this used to seed to , which made "never established" indistinguishable from "tacking away from starboard", so answered for every boat on the start line. Consumers signed control laws by that answer.

member.name: F:Sim.Core.Racing.TackState.Unresolved
member.summary: No determination yet — a boat that has not sailed, or one just re-seated.

member.name: P:Sim.Core.Racing.TackState.Emerging
member.summary: The tack she is on, or is turning onto — and null when she has never established one, which is the answer a caller must handle rather than be handed a guess. Mid-tack it resolves to the tack she is turning onto, which is the one a committing strategist wants.

member.name: T:Sim.Core.Racing.Tack
member.summary: The boat's tack. means it has NO proper tack — from when the bow crosses the wind until it re-establishes at |TWA| ≥ 45°.

member.name: T:Sim.Core.Racing.TackTracker
member.summary: Tracks which tack the boat is sailing, RRS-style, from the signed true-wind angle and the boom yaw, and emits a on each completed tack/gybe. Tack is established by the boom (leeward) side once at a sailing point of sail; the bow crossing the wind is a tack (transient no-tack ), a boom-side flip while established is a gybe. See docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-24-mark-penalties-design.md §5.

member.name: F:Sim.Core.Racing.TackTracker.BoomCommit_rad
member.summary: How far off the centreline the boom must lie before it names a side at all. Inside it the boom is saying nothing, and the tracker holds whatever it last knew.
member.remarks: Measured against the boat, not guessed: a Laser sheeted hard close-hauled settles at 0.058–0.063 rad, and every freer point of sail is far wider (0.20 at 60°, 0.34 on a beam reach, 1.1+ downwind). So the band has to clear the old 0.02 to be worth anything and stay well under 0.058 or a close-hauled boat — the tightest a boom ever sits while sailing — would name no tack at all. It is deliberately NOT the chatter fix: a boom ringing through a gybe swings far wider than any band this side of 0.058, which is what is for.

member.name: F:Sim.Core.Racing.TackTracker.GybeCommit_s
member.summary: How long the boom must hold its new side before that counts as a gybe. A gybe is named by the boom alone — unlike a tack, which also has a head-to-wind crossing to corroborate it — so it is the one transition with no second opinion, and the boom rings across the centreline several times on its way to settling. A gybe takes seconds; a fifth of one costs nothing real.

member.name: P:Sim.Core.Racing.TackTracker.LastEstablished
member.summary: The last tack she actually established, or null if she never has — a boat that has not sailed, or one just re-seated. Null rather than a seeded side, because "never established" and "established to starboard" are different facts and a consumer that cannot tell them apart will invent an answer: used to report port for every boat on a start line, and the AI signs control laws by it.

member.name: P:Sim.Core.Racing.TackTracker.TackState
member.summary: Both facts together — what a consumer needing a definite tack mid-manoeuvre resolves from, so the fallback lives here once instead of at every call site.

member.name: F:Sim.Core.Racing.TackTracker._boomSideSettled
member.summary: The side the boom is deemed to be on — which lags the raw reading by while it is swinging. Held separately from so the raw sample stays available for the head-to-wind logic.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Racing.TackTracker.Update(System.Single,System.Single,System.Single)
member.param: Signed true-wind angle off the bow (+ = wind from port).
Boom yaw (+ swings the boom to port).
Sim time (s), for the gybe's settle window. Monotonic within one boat's run.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Racing.TackTracker.SettledTack
member.summary: The tack the boom is settled on, or null while it is still swinging across.

member.name: T:Sim.Core.Racing.Umpire
member.summary:
The stateful race-level umpire (spec §3): it owns one per boat and one per unordered pair. Each 4 Hz sample it records every boat's snapshot once, then judges the near-pairs it is handed — creating an encounter for any pair not already engaged, stepping it over the two parties' shared windows, and reaping it when it resolves. An encounter whose pair drops out of the near set closes itself from its parties' still-fresh windows.
The per-tick batch shape is what the live wiring (#155) drives from the pairwise pass (#136); recording windows from the boat list (not the pair list) is what keeps a boat in several pairs from being appended more than once.

member.name: P:Sim.Core.Racing.Umpire.ActiveEncounterCount
member.summary: How many pairs are in a live engagement. A spent encounter — already judged, held only until its pair parts so the same incident cannot be billed twice — is not one: it is a receipt, not an engagement.

member.name: P:Sim.Core.Racing.Umpire.LastObservation
member.summary: What this umpire resolved at its most recent — see . before the first one, and again after .

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Racing.Umpire.PairsAt(System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList{System.ValueTuple{Sim.Core.BoatId,Sim.Core.Racing.RrsSnapshot}},System.Single)
member.summary: Every pair in the fleet as this sample resolved them, for the observation.
member.remarks: Built from the FLEET rather than from the near-pairs. A trace wants the whole picture and the near set is the judging gate, not the fleet — and the question a reader most often brings to a trace is why nothing was called, which is answered by the pairs that were never judged.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Racing.Umpire.EncounterViews
member.summary: Every encounter this umpire holds, spent ones included — a spent encounter is why a second foul was not called, which is exactly what a reader querying a quiet sample wants.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Racing.Umpire.Reset
member.summary: Drop every encounter, per-boat window and resolved overlap — the wiring calls this on a race restart so a new race starts with no engagements carried over.
member.remarks: The overlap is the one that had to be said out loud: an encounter and a window hold what happened, and dropping those is obviously right, but the tracker holds what the rule still deems — see for what that costs when it is left behind (#313).

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Racing.Umpire.OverlapAtTheLastSample(Sim.Core.BoatId,Sim.Core.BoatId)
member.summary: This pair's overlap as of the most recent sample, or for a pair that sample did not hold — what a caller capturing a touch between samples judges it by.
member.remarks: A rules question, answered by the rulebook. The caller could read the same fact off , and that would be telemetry feeding back into a decision — the one direction the config/state/telemetry split forbids.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Racing.Umpire.Overlap(System.ValueTuple{Sim.Core.BoatId,Sim.Core.BoatId},System.Single)
member.summary: This pair's resolved overlap, asked in the order the encounter reads its parties — Lo first, because IS the lower-id boat.
member.remarks: The argument order is load-bearing, not stylistic. The relation is directional, so asking it the other way round silently swaps and — and rule 12 would then penalise the boat clear ahead instead of the one astern. Both verdicts are well-formed, so nothing downstream can notice; only the boats would.

member.name: T:Sim.Core.Racing.UmpireObservation
member.summary: Everything the umpire resolved at one sample, read-only and complete — the surface a race trace serialises (#334).

remarks.para: This is the config/state/telemetry taxonomy's "telemetry is read-only out", applied to a record rather than to a live number. The umpire self-describes and gains no writer, no file handle and no knowledge that anything is recording; whether a recorder exists is the host's business.

Rebuilt each sample rather than accumulated. A consumer that wants history keeps its own — which is exactly what a trace file is, and why the umpire does not need to grow one. It also means nothing here outlives the sample it describes, so a reader cannot mistake a stale answer for a current one.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Racing.UmpireObservation.#ctor(System.Single,System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList{Sim.Core.Racing.PairRelation},System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList{Sim.Core.Racing.EncounterView},System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList{Sim.Core.Racing.RulingDetail})

Rebuilt each sample rather than accumulated. A consumer that wants history keeps its own — which is exactly what a trace file is, and why the umpire does not need to grow one. It also means nothing here outlives the sample it describes, so a reader cannot mistake a stale answer for a current one.

member.name: F:Sim.Core.Racing.UmpireObservation.None
member.summary: Before the first sample, and after a reset. Its own value rather than null, so a consumer reads an empty observation instead of branching on whether one has happened yet — and NaN time rather than zero, because a race has a real sample at zero.

member.name: T:Sim.Core.Racing.UmpireSettings
member.summary: The umpire's tunables for the necessity walk-back (spec §3.5, Decision 8). These are the margin + dwell escape hatch against wave/wind jitter; the first cut assumes calm water. Relevance radii are not here — they belong to the gates (Decision 2).

member.name: P:Sim.Core.Racing.UmpireSettings.ContactMargin_m
member.summary: Projected closest approach below which a forced maneuver counts as "would have hit".

member.name: P:Sim.Core.Racing.UmpireSettings.ManeuverAngle_rad
member.summary: Heading change of the right-of-way boat, over the dwell, that reads as a course change.

member.name: P:Sim.Core.Racing.UmpireSettings.ManeuverDwell_s
member.summary: Look-back window for detecting a maneuver and locating the pre-maneuver snapshot.

member.name: P:Sim.Core.Racing.UmpireSettings.MinManeuverSpeed_mps
member.summary: Below this speed a boat's velocity heading is too noisy to call a maneuver from.

member.name: P:Sim.Core.Racing.UmpireSettings.PenaltyTurns
member.summary: Exoneration turns an RRS Part 2 foul owes — Two-Turns by default (spec §3.6). The out-of-zone single-turn variant is a later race-config option keyed here.

member.name: P:Sim.Core.Racing.UmpireSettings.OverlapBreakMargin_m
member.summary: How far past the line abeam a boat must be before an established overlap can break. RRS deems an overlap to stand until it is broken, so the margin is what stops a surge or a wave from ending one — the pair has to genuinely separate, not merely touch the boundary.

member.name: P:Sim.Core.Racing.UmpireSettings.OverlapBreakDwell_s
member.summary: How long that clearance must hold before the overlap is called broken. The margin's partner: together they are the same jitter escape hatch the necessity walk-back uses, and one without the other still breaks on a single clean sample.

member.name: T:Sim.Core.Rendering.FlotsamField
member.summary: Pure placement helper for world-anchored flotsam: one deterministically-jittered point per world grid cell within radius of a centre, with a distance fade. A cell's position depends only on its integer indices and the seed, so it is identical regardless of the centre — the field is world-anchored and recycles automatically as the centre moves. The Godot adapter supplies the centre (camera XY) and displaces each rest point by IWaveField.Displacement. See docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-22-flotsam-motion-cue-design.md.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Rendering.FlotsamField.Build(System.Numerics.Vector2,System.Single,System.Single,System.Int32,System.Single,System.Span{System.Numerics.Vector2},System.Span{System.Single})
member.summary: Fill (rest positions in range) and (1 inside fadeStartFraction·radius → 0 at radius). Returns the number of points written. Caller sizes the spans to the bounding-box cell count (≈ (ceil(2·radius/spacing)+2)²).

member.name: T:Sim.Core.Rendering.WakeBuffer
member.summary: Fixed-capacity ring buffer of : the single source of truth for the wake (docs/wake-design.md §3). Stamps are appended in deposit order; once full, the oldest is overwritten. Pure data — no Godot types — so it lives in Sim.Core alongside and is the same physics/render boundary. The boat solver never reads it; the wake is render-only.

member.name: P:Sim.Core.Rendering.WakeBuffer.Count
member.summary: Number of populated slots (≤ ).

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Rendering.WakeBuffer.Add(Sim.Core.Rendering.WakeStamp@)
member.summary: Append a stamp, overwriting the oldest once the ring is full.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Rendering.WakeBuffer.Clear
member.summary: Drop every stamp (e.g. on a sim reset / time jump).

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Rendering.WakeBuffer.WriteActive(System.Single,System.Single,System.Single,System.Span{Sim.Core.Rendering.WakeQuad})
member.summary: Resolve the live wake at time into : every populated stamp still alive (age in [0, max(foamLifetime, swirlLifetime))) is advected by its drift and written as a . Foam and swirl fade on independent timescales — foam (the bright churn) on the shorter so it stays near-field, swirl (the disturbed strip) on the longer . Stamps past both lifetimes, or with a future birth-time (after a backward time jump), are skipped. Returns the number written; if fills first the remaining stamps are dropped and the count is capped.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Rendering.WakeBuffer.Decay(System.Single)
member.summary: Foam fade over normalized age ∈ [0,1]: 1 at birth → 0 at the lifetime, with an ease-out tail (quadratic) so foam lingers then thins rather than cutting off.

member.name: T:Sim.Core.Rendering.WakeStamp
member.summary: One Lagrangian wake deposit, frozen in world coordinates at . The hull stamps a small set of these per deposit (transom + quarters, see ); once stamped a sample never moves with the boat — it advects only by its own (≈0 on flat water) and fades with age. The boat then drives away from its own wake, which is what makes leeway, turning, and sideslip fall out for free. See docs/wake-design.md §3.
member.remarks: Two channels ride on the same stamp because they are physically different and feed different renderers: is a surface property (aerated whiteness, Phase 1, soft quads) and is geometry (water pushed down/up, Phase 2, summed into the wave field). Phase 1 only writes ; is carried from day one so Phase 2 is "turn it on", not a rewrite.
member.param: World position on the z=0 plane where the disturbance was deposited.
Environment time (s) at deposit; age = t − BirthTime drives decay.
Initial foam intensity [0..1] (aerated whiteness, driven by wave-making drag — only appears near the hull-speed hump). Decays to 0 over the lifetime.

Initial swirl intensity [0..1] (disturbed-water ripple, driven by *speed* — present whenever the boat is moving, including slowly). The render-only approximation of churned water under the foam. Decays to 0 over the lifetime.
Initial displacement amplitude (m), signed: <0 trough, >0 hump. Phase 2.
Kernel radius (m); grows with hull beam and speed.
Advection velocity (m/s) of this sample; ≈0 on flat/Airy water.

member.name: T:Sim.Core.Rendering.WakeSourcePoint
member.summary: One hull source point in body frame (docs/wake-design.md §4): a place on the wetted footprint that stamps wake. scales this point's foam relative to the transom (1.0); scales the kernel radius (transom band wider than the feathery arms); is the displacement polarity for Phase 2 (−1 trough at the transom, +1 hump at the bow / divergent crests at the quarters) and is unused while only foam ships. An off-centre point (|.Y| > 0) is treated as a divergent arm: its deposits drift outboard with age so the trail fans into a Kelvin-angle V (see ).
