member.name: T:Sim.Core.Rendering.WakeConfig
member.summary: Tunable wake constants. Defaults are Phase-1 sensible for the ILCA; the Godot adapter overrides and from the hull mesh and exposes the scalar knobs on the "Wake" config panel (docs/wake-design.md §12). The scalars are set so the panel can mutate them live; reads them every deposit. and are fixed at construction (the ring buffer is sized once).

member.name: P:Sim.Core.Rendering.WakeConfig.Spacing_m
member.summary: Stamp a new deposit set whenever the boat has moved this far — constant *spatial* spacing, so wake density is speed- and frame-rate-independent (§5).

member.name: P:Sim.Core.Rendering.WakeConfig.MaxLifetime_s
member.summary: Trail lifetime (s): the swirl/disturbed-water strip fades to zero by this age, and stamps are recycled past it. The long timescale.

member.name: P:Sim.Core.Rendering.WakeConfig.FoamLifetime_s
member.summary: Foam lifetime (s): the bright aerated foam fades by this (shorter) age, so foam stays a near-field churn at the transom/rudder and the long trail is just disturbed water — not speckle.

member.name: P:Sim.Core.Rendering.WakeConfig.FoamDragRef_N
member.summary: Wave drag (N) mapping to full foam. Foam tracks WaveDragMagnitude_N, not raw speed, so brightness swells through the hull-speed hump and thins as planing cuts residuary drag (§5). ~Peak ILCA wave drag.

member.name: P:Sim.Core.Rendering.WakeConfig.RadiusBase_m
member.summary: Base kernel radius (m) at rest; set from hull beam by the adapter.

member.name: P:Sim.Core.Rendering.WakeConfig.RadiusFroudeGain
member.summary: Kernel radius widens by this × Froude (wider, flatter trail when planing).

member.name: P:Sim.Core.Rendering.WakeConfig.SwirlSpeedFull_m_s
member.summary: Speed (m/s) at which the swirl channel saturates: swirl = clamp(speed / this). Drives the disturbed-water ripple, which (unlike foam) is present even at slow speed — so there is always a wake when the boat moves. Lower = swirl saturates sooner.

member.name: P:Sim.Core.Rendering.WakeConfig.ArmSpreadFactor
member.summary: Outboard spread of the divergent arms as a fraction of boat speed: an arm stamp drifts sideways at speed × ArmSpreadFactor, so over distance the trail fans into a V of half-angle atan(ArmSpreadFactor). 0.34 ≈ the 19° Kelvin half-angle; smaller reads as a tighter foam wash.

member.name: P:Sim.Core.Rendering.WakeConfig.HeelAsymmetry
member.summary: Heel (roll) asymmetry strength [0..1]: at full heel the leeward (downhill) divergent arm is brightened/fattened by this fraction and the windward arm thinned by it — the hull buries the leeward quarter. 0 = symmetric. Driven by Roll_rad (positive = heeled to starboard, so leeward is the −y / starboard side).

member.name: P:Sim.Core.Rendering.WakeConfig.RollFull_rad
member.summary: Heel angle (rad) at which the asymmetry reaches full strength (~20° = 0.35 rad).

member.name: P:Sim.Core.Rendering.WakeConfig.Capacity
member.summary: Ring-buffer capacity. ≥ (MaxLifetime · maxSpeed / Spacing) · |Sources| with headroom.

member.name: T:Sim.Core.Rendering.WakeSystem
member.summary: World-anchored Lagrangian wake deposition (docs/wake-design.md §1, §5). Each , once the boat has travelled since the last deposit, stamps the configured into the at their *current world* transform. Because the hull is yawed to its heading but its world position tracks along the course over ground, the stamp trail streams off at the leeway angle (crabbing) and curls on turns with no special-casing — the wake is just the locus of where the hull has been. Pure; the renderer owns the mesh.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Rendering.WakeSystem.Update(Sim.Core.Rendering.WakeSample@)
member.summary: Deposit if the boat has moved ≥ since the last stamp set.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Rendering.WakeSystem.Reset
M:Sim.Core.Rendering.WakeSystem.DefaultSources(System.Single,System.Single,System.Single)
member.summary: Convenience: source points for a hull of the given waterline length / beam — transom centre (main foam trail) plus the two quarters (divergent Kelvin arms). / are the body-frame fore-aft extents (x forward); the quarters sit a short way forward of the transom at ±beam/2.

member.name: T:Sim.Core.Rig.CamberSection
member.summary: Geometry of a 2-D sail-strip camber line — a single-hump mean line of two circular arcs with maximum camber at a fixed chord position , parameterised by draft depth f = max camber ÷ chord. Pure geometry: converts between cloth (arc) length and depth (the skin-length machinery) and exposes the thin-airfoil zero-lift angle and the soft-sail centre of pressure the aero needs. No dependencies. See spec 2026-06-08-cambered-strips-design §1.

member.name: P:Sim.Core.Rig.CamberSection.Position
member.summary: Draft position (fraction of chord aft of the luff) of the max camber. Fixed at 0.35 for now; becomes tension-driven later.

member.name: F:Sim.Core.Rig.CamberSection.DesignDepth
member.summary: Draft depth at which the (non-separable two-arc) normalized shape G and its thin-airfoil constants are evaluated. Fixed at the design camber for now (matches LaserDefaults).

member.name: P:Sim.Core.Rig.CamberSection.ArcConstant
member.summary: C in arcRatio ≈ 1 + C·f² (= ½∫₀¹ g'(x)² dx). ~3.02 at p=0.35 (two-arc).

member.name: P:Sim.Core.Rig.CamberSection.ZeroLiftConstant
member.summary: A in α0 = −A·f (thin-airfoil zero-lift). ~1.77 at p=0.35 (two-arc).

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Rig.CamberSection.LeechEdgeAngle_rad(System.Single)
member.summary: Tangent angle (rad) the camber line makes with the chord at the LEECH (trailing edge) for a given draft depth: atan(depth·|g'(1)|). This is the angle the membrane edge tension acts along at the leech — shallow for a forward draft position.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Rig.CamberSection.LuffEdgeAngle_rad(System.Single)
member.summary: Tangent angle (rad) the camber line makes with the chord at the LUFF (leading edge) for a given draft depth: atan(depth·|g'(0)|). Steeper than the leech for a forward draft. Used (as a scalar) in the membrane perpendicular balance, not as a force direction.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Rig.CamberSection.CamberLine(System.Single,System.Single)
member.summary: Camber-line height at chord fraction ∈ [0,1] for a draft depth — two circular arcs meeting with a horizontal tangent at the apex (Position, depth). Single source of truth for the section shape (aero/membrane geometry AND the renderer). Flat for depth ≈ 0.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Rig.CamberSection.ArcLengthRatio(System.Single)
member.summary: Arc length of the cambered mean line (depth f) over a unit chord, ≥ 1 (exact, numeric).

member.name: F:Sim.Core.Rig.CamberSection.MaxInvertibleDepth
member.summary: Deepest draft this section can reliably invert. The two-arc is non-monotonic — it turns over around this draft — so the Newton inverse below is only single-valued under it. Far above any real/clamped sail draft (design ~0.11), so this is a defensive saturation, not an operating limit.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Rig.CamberSection.DepthFromArcLengthRatio(System.Single)
member.summary: Depth that yields this cloth-over-chord ratio (inverse of ). Newton from the small-camber seed √((ratio−1)/C). Flat (0) for ratio ≤ 1; saturated at for ratios past the (two-arc) arc-length turning point.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Rig.CamberSection.ZeroLiftAngle_rad(System.Single)
member.summary: Thin-airfoil zero-lift angle (rad): α0 = −A·depth.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Rig.CamberSection.CentreOfPressureFraction(System.Single,System.Single)
member.summary: Chord fraction aft of the luff where the resultant acts. Near 0.40 of the chord at full lift (soft-sail band), running aft toward ~0.47 near the luff; deeper camber nudges it aft a touch. Clamped to [0.38, 0.48].

member.name: T:Sim.Core.Rig.IMastShape

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Rig.IMastShape.PointAtHeight_B(System.Single)

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Rig.IMastShape.TangentAtHeight_B(System.Single)
member.summary: Unit body-frame tangent of the mast centreline at a height above the gooseneck — the local luff direction a strip twists about. Vertical (+z) for a straight mast; tilts with rake/bend for a bending one.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Rig.IMastShape.PointAtArcLength_B(System.Single)
member.summary: Body-frame mast position at a cloth-arc length along the (possibly bent) centreline, measured from the gooseneck. For a straight mast arc ≡ height. Consumers (the sail) place luff nodes by the cut's cumulative luff-arc so the head foreshortens correctly as the mast bends.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Rig.IMastShape.Integrate(System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList{Sim.Core.Rig.MastLoad},System.Single)
member.summary: Advance the mast as a dynamic element by under this tick's published loads. The mast is a damped rig component (like the boom): the sail reads its shape via (lagged one tick), then calls this once per tick to step it forward. ≤ 0 ⇒ no advance.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Rig.IMastShape.SetRigLoads_B(System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList{Sim.Core.Rig.MastLoad})
member.summary:
Latch what the boom and its running rigging hang on the mast, each at its own height, applied on every subsequent until set again. The runner latches these AFTER the boom solve, so the mast sees them next tick — the same one-tick lag as the shape the sail reads.
Separate from 's loads only because they arrive out of band: the sail owns the tick in which the mast integrates, so the boom's contribution cannot be handed over in-line. Same currency, same treatment once inside.
Implementations must COPY: the runner reuses its buffer between ticks.

member.name: P:Sim.Core.Rig.IMastShape.InertialComponent
member.summary: The mast's lumped mass distribution as a body-fixed rigid component (mass, body-frame CoM, principal inertia), summed into the boat aggregate alongside the hull, sails, and boom. A mast is its own rigid body rigidly stepped into the hull — this is what used to be folded into the hull model's inertia. default (zero mass) contributes nothing.

member.name: T:Sim.Core.Rig.RigidMast
member.summary: Undeflected mast: a straight vertical line above the gooseneck. The default everywhere, reproducing pre-bend behaviour bit-for-bit. is a no-op.

Per design-doc §17 sail-level composition, each sail is its own model in ; the sim always calls every sail's regardless of mode (the sail itself decides whether it's Doused, Flying, Luffing, Stalled, or Collapsed — Task 6).

member.name: T:Sim.Core.Rig.LeechNodeState
member.summary: Per-leech-node state. A leech-string runs from each node to the next; the panel-discretised sail model exposes PanelCount + 1 nodes (0 = clew, N = head). Per spec §6.7.
member.param: Node position in world frame at the current twist solution — the REAL (roachy) corner a renderer draws: the tension path below plus the cut's rigid roach overlay.
Tension in the leech-string segment from this node going up to the next. The top node (head) reports 0 (no segment above).

The de-roached node the solver actually works on, world frame — where the leech string runs, before the battened roach is laid over it. Published alongside the real corner because the roach is a pure function of this, the luff and the static cut (RoachOverlay), so a consumer holding it can rebuild the real edge but not the other way round: the chord that StripDraft measures is this one, and feeding it the roachy corner instead collapses draft to zero. Identity on a cut with no roach.

member.summary: Component, about a luff axis (body frame), of the torque a leech-string segment applies. The string at pulls toward with magnitude ; the torque is taken about and projected onto . Returns 0 for a degenerate (zero-length) segment or non-positive tension.

member.name: T:Sim.Core.Rig.OuthaulClewGeometry
member.summary: Outhaul clew geometry. The clew rides on the boom; its FLAT (most-outboard) position is set by the foot CLOTH, not the boom tip — a foot cut shorter than the boom simply can't span to the tip. Easing the outhaul slides the clew inboard from flat, pulling the foot chord below the cloth → foot camber. When the foot cut equals the boom length this reduces to clew-to-tip = ease (the historical behaviour, so the stock Laser and its tests are unchanged).

member.name: P:Sim.Core.Rig.RigGeometry.BridleLength_m

member.name: P:Sim.Core.Rig.RigGeometry.MastheadAboveDeck_m
member.summary: Masthead height above the deck (z = 0). The mast is stepped .Z *below* the deck and is step-to-tip, so the two do not simply add to the visible height — this does. It doubles as a bending mast's cantilever length, because the deck partner is where the mast is clamped.

member.name: P:Sim.Core.Rig.RigGeometry.LuffSpan_m
member.summary: Masthead measured from the gooseneck — the sail's luff span, and the top of the range is asked for.

member.name: P:Sim.Core.Rig.RigGeometry.DeckAboveGooseneck_m
member.summary: Where the deck sits in the above-gooseneck heights speaks — negative, the gooseneck being above the deck. This is the **bottom of the mast**, not the gooseneck: a bending mast is clamped at the deck and its centreline starts there, so anything drawing or measuring the whole spar starts here rather than at height 0.

member.name: P:Sim.Core.Rig.RigGeometry.VangTangAboveGooseneck_m
member.summary: Where the vang's mast-side tang sits in above-gooseneck heights — negative, the tang being below the gooseneck. Despite the name, is a fitting on the MAST (Laser: on the mast axis, 95 mm above the deck), so the vang is a two-force member internal to the mast+boom system and its pull must be booked against the mast here, not lost into the hull.

member.name: T:Sim.Core.Rig.SailCut
member.summary: A parsed sail-cut file (see the parametric-sail-cut spec). Carries the generator's design inputs (provenance), the model-ready per-panel data, and derived quantities, and projects them onto the sim types and . Phase 1 ignores the draft fields. Written by tools/SailCutGen; read here.
member.remarks:
The JSON-mapped properties are set, not init, and that is load-bearing. Source generation cannot call an init accessor, so it emulates one as a constructor parameter and assigns every such property on every construction — an omitted key then overwrites the property initializer with default(T). A cut that leaves out an optional key would silently load nulls (see SailCutSparseJsonTests).
The setters are internal, and that is load-bearing too. is a process-wide singleton — every boat in the process composes from that one instance — so a public setter would let any consumer re-cut every sail in the sim. init used to prevent exactly that and cannot be used here, so the accessor is narrowed instead of opened. [JsonInclude] is what lets source generation reach a non-public accessor; without it the generator skips the property entirely and the cut loads empty.

member.name: P:Sim.Core.Rig.SailCut.MeshBlock.LeechSegmentVirtual_m
member.summary:
Flying rest between consecutive VIRTUAL (de-roached) leech nodes — THE per-segment leech rest, and the only one the cut carries. N values.
A pre-roach-split cut has no such block: it carried only the real (roachy) leech segments, which the virtual-leech solver cannot use as a rest. Rather than silently reinterpret them, such a cut fails to project () — regenerate it with the designer.

member.name: T:Sim.Core.Rig.SailCutSource
member.summary: Resolves the sim's active sail cut. With NO path configured the embedded canonical is the deliberate default. But a path that IS configured and then turns out missing or malformed is a hard error — we throw rather than silently substitute a different sail (a stale/absent cut quietly falling back to a default has bitten us before). The caller decides whether to surface or recover; the resolver never guesses.

member.name: T:Sim.Core.Rig.SailInputs
member.summary: Per-sail sailor controls for one tick. Per design-doc §17.3.
member.remarks:
Per design-doc §3.5 (refined by the spanwise-rig spec §2), the mainsheet is a length-input, tension-output system. The sailor pays out / pulls in a geometric length and the Boom (added by the dynamic-boom work) computes the constraint reaction as the sheet tension on its .
v1: bail-to-block distance, vang control length, and an Active flag. Future inputs (cunningham, outhaul, traveler, jib sheet, ...) land as additional fields when their physics arrive. The input is the rest length of the vang spring inside the Boom (length-input contract symmetric with the sheet).
member.param: Geometric distance from the boom bail to the centerline sheet block, in meters. Rest length of the sheet spring inside the Boom. Per spec §2.
Geometric distance from the vang's hull-side attach to its boom-side attach, in meters. Use for "no vang / slack vang."

True when the sail is hoisted and contributing aero; false when doused / struck (returns Mode=Doused, zero forces). Per §17.3, the sail decides its internal sub-model based on Active and apparent wind.

Distance from boom tip to clew (metres); the clew rides on the boom so tension acts along the boom. Default ≈ 0.079 m (= Foot_m − Foot_m/ArcLengthRatio(0.11), two-arc) — the C1 design draft position for the canonical cut's foot (2.35 m). Increasing eases the foot and adds depth; decreasing flattens it. Hand-synced with LaserDefaults.OuthaulDesign_m; guarded by OuthaulTests.

member.name: T:Sim.Core.Rig.SailMeasurements
member.summary:
The three sail EDGE cloth lengths (the cloth perimeter), in metres. These are distinct from a panel's chord (the straight luff→leech aero reference line): an edge/skin length exceeds its chord whenever there is draft, since the camber bags the cloth out behind the chord. Aero always uses the chord, never these skin lengths.
These are REPORTED cloth measurements — they are not what the leech reads. The one-sided leech twist constraint takes its per-segment rest straight from the cut mesh (): the tension path is the de-roached virtual leech, whereas is the arc along the real, roachy edge. The two differ by the roach — battened cloth carried OUTSIDE the tension path — so scaling a rest to would invent slack. seeds the outhaul design travel; is reported only.
Defaults () are the ILCA 7 (Laser Standard) class measurements from the 2026-06-04 handbook research: luff 5.130 m, leech 5.570 m, foot 2.740 m.

member.name: P:Sim.Core.Rig.SailMesh.Roach_m

member.name: P:Sim.Core.Rig.SailMesh.SkinVirtual_m
member.summary: Option A.5: de-roached "virtual" skin (m) — luff node → leech node projected onto the straight leech line. The chordwise cloth on the structural tension path (camber rides this). N+1.

member.name: P:Sim.Core.Rig.SailMesh.LeechSegmentVirtual_m
member.summary:
Flying rest between consecutive VIRTUAL (de-roached) leech nodes — THE per-segment leech rest. N values.
The de-roached rest is the only one there is: the leech solves on the virtual (straight-line) tension path, and the roach is battened cloth carried outside it as an overlay (). The real (roachy) leech segments this cut used to also carry were never a rest the solver could use — being longer, they left the virtual leech permanently slack — so they are gone rather than kept as a trap.

member.name: T:Sim.Core.Rig.SailShape
member.summary:
Static sail planform for panel-discretised sail models. Per spanwise-rig spec §5.
The sail is divided into equal-span panels stacked along the luff. [i] is the chord at the bottom edge of panel i, normalized to the foot length (= RigGeometry.BoomLength_m). Element 0 is always 1.0 (the foot). Panel boundaries are at span fractions i / N of the luff height.
is the chord at the top of the topmost panel (the head). Default 0 (triangular sail; topmost panel collapses to a triangle). Reserved for square-headed sails.
Roach is encoded by non-linearly decreasing fractions, e.g. [1.0, 0.8, 0.65, 0.35] for a 4-panel sail with leech roach (vs. triangular [1.0, 0.75, 0.5, 0.25]).

member.name: T:Sim.Core.Runner.ForceDiagnostics
member.summary: Per-source force/moment breakdown for diagnostics and visualisation. Carries the totals and the per-component contributions that summed to those totals.

remarks.para: The per-source breakdown is consumed by the component test bench (design doc §13) and is available for any future per-source display in the live-sail scene. All moments in are about the same reference as — conventionally BoatState.Position_W.

Per §21, the record also carries the boat-wide aggregate parasitic drag, induced drag, and buoyancy magnitudes — summed across hull and appendages. The renderer's force-overlay can use these to toggle "parasitic drag" vs "induced drag" without re-deriving them from the per-source breakdown.

member.name: T:Sim.Core.Runner.ForceEvaluation
member.summary: Shared per-tick force-and-moment evaluation, used by both (which then advances the boom and integrates) and the test-only bench evaluator (which does not integrate). One source of truth for how component forces compose into a net force and moment, and for the per-component breakdown reported in .

remarks.para: Uses one per component so each component's net force and moment can be reported separately. The grand totals are simple sums of the per- component totals, which is mathematically identical to the old single-aggregator version because is linear.

Boom dynamics and the torque-translation-to-CG step intentionally remain in ; this helper only iterates the per-role force contributors and reports totals + per-source breakdown + per-component state snapshots.

member.name: T:Sim.Core.Runner.ISimHost
member.summary:
The embeddable contract for one simulated boat-entity: advance it a tick, read its published output, and discover its self-described surfaces — with no Godot (or any engine) dependency, so a host game engine can drive the sim through this alone. Implemented by .
The config / state / telemetry taxonomy is enforced here: the only two-way state surface is the per-tick control passed to (the sim owns and republishes it); configuration is read via (each is read/write, but changed deliberately, not per tick); telemetry is the read-only plus the discoverable .
World-ready shape: a future world owns N hosts sharing one , so this contract is per-entity and takes the shared medium by reference rather than owning it. Debug-bench controls (mode, boom lock, analysis-body override, rebuild) stay off this interface, on the concrete .

member.name: T:Sim.Core.Runner.SettleSolver
member.summary:
Pre-rolls a boat to its steady sailing state so the live sim (and reset) can start there rather than from an upright/at-rest pose — eliminating the startup heel swing the user otherwise sees as the boat snaps into its wind-induced heel and overshoots.
Steps a (Live mode) on the given boat instance, so the boat's swings out and settles in place (abeam, if the eased sheet allows) as a side effect — no boom-state plumbing needed. Run it against a flat wave field for a clean, wave-free equilibrium. Deterministic; no Godot dependency.
Steady state is detected by small linear acceleration (constant speed) and small angular velocity (no rotation) sustained for several steps — not zero linear velocity, since under wind the boat sails forward at a steady speed. Always terminates at maxSteps.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Runner.SimRunner.Step(Sim.Core.Dynamics.BoatState@,System.Single,Sim.Core.Rig.SailInputs,Sim.Core.Appendage.AppendageInputs,Sim.Core.Crew.CrewInputs)
member.summary: Advance state by one tick at simulation time with the given sailor controls. The returned state corresponds to time + . Full per-tick snapshot is published on .
member.remarks:
Delegates to the privately-owned . The body and time are passed in per call (SimRunner is stateless w.r.t. the body and time), so each step re-initialises the session's and step clock from and via , and forces Live mode.
The caller-supplied is authoritative: the session is reseeded from it each call, so it drives wind/wave sampling and the published .Time (= + ), regardless of how many prior steps the session has taken. This restores the original SimRunner contract and lets an external caller reset time (e.g. the Godot UI "R" reset, which zeroes its sim-time accumulator without rebuilding the runner) without the session's internal counter drifting out of sync.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Runner.SimSession.AdoptBoat(Sim.Core.Boat.Boat)
member.summary:
Sail a freshly composed boat from the next tick (e.g. after a sail-cut reload). Re-bootstraps the aggregate cache; the boom and the sail's leech warm-start are owned by the new boat, so they start clean.
The caller hands the boat in; this session does not compose one. It used to hold its own factory and recompose behind everyone's back, which meant a host could swap the boat while whoever owned the rest of that composition — the mast, the sail model — went on holding the parts of a boat the sim no longer stepped. Sim.World.BoatEntity.Rebuild is the one door now, and it moves the whole composition together.

member.name: M:Sim.Core.Runner.SimSession.LatchRigLoadsOnMast(Sim.Core.Dynamics.BoatState@)
member.summary:
Hand the mast what the boom and its running rigging hang on it. Two loads, at two heights: the hinge reaction at the gooseneck, and the vang's own pull on its mast tang half a metre lower. The mast picks them up on the next tick's Integrate (it integrates earlier in the tick, inside the sail): a one-tick lag, matching the lagged shape the sail already reads.
The vang is internal to the mast+boom system, so it must appear at BOTH ends or not at all. Booking only the gooseneck end pushes the mast with a force that has no reaction anywhere — what the mast should feel is the couple between the two. The arm is short (the tang is 95 mm above the deck against a gooseneck at 595 mm), so this trims the vang's bending term by ~2.6 % rather than cancelling it.
Sheet, vang and boom weight appear nowhere in MastLoadAssembler, so this cannot double-count the sail aero. The clew force is still excluded — it shares the segment-0 leech tension already published to the mast (issue #262).
The line forces read here are the start-of-tick ones Boom.Build captured, not post-solve: ApplyAcceleration recomputes geometry at the pose it was entered with and assigns the new BoomState afterwards, so nothing refreshes them and latching earlier would give identical numbers. See the P3 spec §1.

member.summary: This boat's tack and the last one she established, together — the pair a consumer needs to resolve a definite tack while she is mid-manoeuvre. Spelled as two parameters rather than one because a record's default must be a compile-time constant, and a defaulted struct here would read as .

member.name: F:Sim.Core.Runner.SimState.CurrentSchemaVersion
member.summary:
Schema version. Bump on any non-additive change to or any nested record. See design-doc §16.2.1 for bump rules.
v2 was the §16/§17 sail-composition migration. v3 (spanwise-rig spec) added and dropped the BoomAngle_rad / SheetTension_N / VangTension_N mirrors from . v4 (component test bench) extends with a per-source Sources list of entries. v5 (spanwise-rig Plan 2) adds LeechNodes to and the leech-solver diagnostics (since removed — see v9). v6 adds AeroForce_W to so consumers can render per-panel force vectors without re-deriving direction from Normal_W + drag. v7 adds — the sliding sheet-bridle block state (default/zero for boats with no traveler). v8 added AssistMoment_Nm — the roll moment applied by the anti-capsize assist (since removed — see v11). v9 drops Diagnostics. Its leech-solver fields were fed only by the fixed-leech sail model's Gauss-Seidel solver; that model is gone, so every field had become a hardcoded default — a reading a host could mistake for a real measurement. v10 adds — the rudder blade's integrated stock angle + rate (§39's 1-DOF blade), mirroring . v11 drops AssistMoment_Nm with the anti-capsize assist itself: an invented restoring moment is a difficulty setting, not physics, and it masked real heel behaviour. v12 adds + . The boat derives her own tack once, here, instead of the race and the AI each deriving one that disagreed with the other's through the tacking interval. v13 makes nullable. Seeding it to a side made "never established" indistinguishable from "tacking away from starboard", so every boat on a start line resolved as being on port — and consumers signed control laws by that. v14 adds TensionPathPosition_W to — the de-roached node the leech solver works on, beside the roachy corner already published. Draft is measured against that chord, so a consumer given only the roachy one cannot recover it. v15 adds SheetLimits / VangLimits to — the crew-pull cap and purchase of each control line, published beside the tensions they bound. Without them a consumer can read a load but not how close to the crew's limit it is, which is what an AI trimmer needs to haul at a human's speed rather than a winch's.
